articles.title: Mikel Arteta praises Arsenal players for ‘remarkable’ start to the season
articles.summary: Mike Arteta has spoken after Arsenal’s 1-0 win over Hull.
articles.content:
Mikel Arteta praises Arsenal players for ‘remarkable’ start to the season

Mike Arteta has spoken after Arsenal’s 1-0 win over Hull.

Last Update:

Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta has hailed his players for their remarkable run of performances ahead of the international break, while admitting he was confused by a controversial penalty decision in the 1-0 win over Hull on Saturday.

Speaking to BBC Match of the Day after the final whistle, Arteta praised his squad for maintaining their standards during a demanding run of fixtures.

“Very happy with the performance and the victory as well. I think it is time to praise my players,” he said.

“What they have done not only today but after the international break is remarkable because of the games.

“We had to wait and be patient in the last part of the game to make the difference and win the game,” he explained.

“We kept generating chances, the final pass was missing or the last shot was blocked.

“We said at half-time if this is the case it will go all the way to full time but at some point it would come.”

Despite being pleased with Arsenal’s attacking play, Arteta believes there is still room for improvement when it comes to converting opportunities.

“We have some great moments, we need to put the chances we are creating against the opponent into the scoreline,” he added.

“That is what we need to improve.”

Arsenal boss questions confusing penalty decision

Arteta also addressed a controversial refereeing decision after Arsenal were denied a penalty following a VAR review.

Kai Havertz was pulled down in the penalty box, but was not awarded a penalty due to the German being in an offside position.

Arteta was left uncertain about the explanation after an offside decision prevented Arsenal from being awarded the spot-kick.

“I don’t know. When they called the referee to the monitor I thought it was a penalty but then I heard the decision was made because of the offside decision,” Arteta said.

“We don’t have clarity on it.”

articles.title: Daniel Farke claims Jayden Bogle a ‘butterfly’ after defender escapes red card in Leeds’ win over Tottenham
articles.summary: Daniel Farke says Jayden Bogle should not have been sent off against Tottenham.
articles.content:
Daniel Farke claims Jayden Bogle a ‘butterfly’ after defender escapes red card in Leeds’ win over Tottenham

Daniel Farke says Jayden Bogle should not have been sent off against Tottenham.

Last Update:

Leeds United manager Daniel Farke has defended Jayden Bogle following his challenge on Mathys Tel during Saturday’s 1-0 win over Tottenham, insisting the defender had no intention of hurting the Spurs forward.

Bogle came under scrutiny after a collision with Tel left the Tottenham player injured, but Farke was quick to dismiss suggestions that his defender had acted maliciously.

The Leeds boss described Bogle as one of the gentlest players in the Premier League, revealing that he affectionately refers to him as his “butterfly”.

Speaking to TNT Sports after the match, Farke was asked about Bogle’s involvement in the incident that left Tel injured.

“I haven’t watched it back. I have heard there were several doubtful situations. A possible hand ball,” Farke said.

“I just know that Jayden Bogle out of any bad intention. It looked like a coming together.

“It’s very unlucky outcome that Mathys is injured and we wish him all the best and he can recover quickly,” he added.

“The last thing Jayden Bogle is a nasty player. He’s possibly the softest player in the whole league.”

The Leeds manager then revealed the nickname he has given the defender, insisting it reflects his personality.

“I always call him my butterfly, and I can guarantee it was never out of bad intention.”

Leeds boss hails ‘fully deserved’ Tottenham win

Despite the controversy surrounding Bogle’s challenge, Farke was delighted with his side’s performance as Leeds secured all three points against Tottenham.

“We were pushing to win this game and were relentless,” Farke said.

“We showed great spirit, commitment and unity. It was a fully deserved win.”

articles.title: Venezia win battle at bottom of Serie A, Gladbach’s sorry start continues in Bundesliga
articles.summary: Venezia claimed their second win through a stunning decisive goal.
articles.content:
Venezia win battle at bottom of Serie A, Gladbach’s sorry start continues in Bundesliga

Venezia claimed their second win through a stunning decisive goal.

Last Update:

Kike Perez scored a stunning winner to help Venezia move off the bottom of Serie A as they leapfrogged Udinese with a 2-1 home victory.

Udinese have been mainstays in Serie A since their promotion back to the top flight in 1995. However, they appear to be in significant danger of relegation this season.

Indeed, I Friulani are now rock bottom of the table following their latest defeat, which marked their eighth of the season.

Venezia took the lead eight minutes into the second half when Toma Basic slotted home, only for Matias Moreno’s own goal to level matters.

However, Perez sealed the points for Venezia in style, his effort from a little over 20 yards bending beautifully into the top-right corner.

In the Bundesliga, Borussia Monchengladbach remain at the foot of the table after a 3-1 defeat at Hamburg.

Miro Muheim’s long-range effort put Hamburg in front, but Gladbach were given hope of a rare positive result just before half-time when Joe Scally’s strike deflected in off team-mate Robin Hack.

Yet Ko Itakura’s second yellow card four minutes into the second half reduced Gladbach to 10 men, and Hamburg took advantage with goals from Shafiq Nandja and Albert Gronbaek.

Elsewhere, Sevilla and Alaves drew 0-0 in LaLiga, while Toulouse beat Strasbourg 3-1 in Ligue 1.

articles.title: ‘I’m at peace with my decision’ – Portugal boss feels no guilt over Ronaldo retirement
articles.summary: Jesus broke his silence on Ronaldo's abrupt end to his international career.
articles.content:
‘I’m at peace with my decision’ – Portugal boss feels no guilt over Ronaldo retirement

Jesus broke his silence on Ronaldo's abrupt end to his international career.

Last Update:

Portugal boss Jorge Jesus insisted he does not feel guilt over his part in the saga that preceded Cristiano Ronaldo‘s retirement from international football.

Ronaldo, whose 146 international goals mark an all-time record, announced his retirement from Portugal duty this week.

The Al-Nassr star made his final appearance for Portugal in September’s 1-0 Nations League win over Wales, before Jesus’ decision to leave Ronaldo as an unused substitute in their subsequent game with Norway sparked the row that essentially ended the 41-year-old’s international career.

Having gone straight down the tunnel after being left on the bench for the win over Norway, Ronaldo left the Portugal camp in Copenhagen on the eve of their clash with Denmark.

Ronaldo, who accused Jesus of breaking his word, was fined €255 (£215; $286) and given a 30-day ban by the Portuguese Football Federation.

It was expected that conciliatory talks would see Ronaldo return for Portugal’s final Nations League group games with Denmark and Wales this month.

But he instead elected to quit, though Jesus has no regrets.

Jesus, who also previously worked with Ronaldo at Al-Nassr, said: “Maybe I rushed things, but [his retirement was] not because of me. It was in his head, more call-ups, fewer call-ups.

“We also talked about it a few times. And if it was going to happen. But no, I don’t feel guilty about anything regarding his departure. I respect his decision.

“And, as such, his story cannot be ignored. He will always be a symbol and I have built a strong friendship with him over this year and a half.”

Jesus confirmed he planned to select Ronaldo for the upcoming games and had no advance warning about his retirement.

“I found out when we all did,” Jesus added. “Until then, I knew nothing about it.

“He was playing, he was scoring goals; he was one of the players on my squad list.

“All my decisions were made with the team in mind. As a manager, I have always defended what was best for the team. I am at peace with my decision.”

articles.title: Premier League Predictions: Manchester United and Chelsea frustrated but Arsenal, City and Liverpool march on
articles.summary: It's week 10 and there are some exciting games to watch out for. Here are our Premier League predictions for this weekend...
articles.content:
Premier League Predictions: Manchester United and Chelsea frustrated but Arsenal, City and Liverpool march on

It's week 10 and there are some exciting games to watch out for. Here are our Premier League predictions for this weekend...

Last Update:

We are on the eve of another Premier League weekend with some fantastic games to come.

Can Arsenal retain top spot ahead of Manchester City? Will Brighton maintain their blistering domestic form and can rock-bottom Sunderland surprise Chelsea?

Here, we list this weekend’s games and give our Premier League predictions!

FRIDAY

Everton v Coventry (8pm)Everton looked strong at Newcastle on Monday night and it may be the decision to ostracise Jack Grealish from the squad has galvanised the rest of the players. With Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall shining in midfield and Thierno Barry continuing to defy the critics and score goals, the Toffees are moving in the right direction. The same can be said for Coventry, who have won three of their last five league games to climb out of the bottom three. It is a tough ask for them tonight, though, and we fancy David Moyes to mark his record-equalling 592nd game in charge of Everton with a win.Prediction: Everton 2-0 Coventry

SATURDAY

Leeds v Tottenham (12.30pm)The mood at Tottenham has changed completely following three successive wins and they will head to Elland Road in confident mood. This is a good test of the ‘new Spurs’ under Roberto De Zerbi with the hosts strong at home. Leeds are on a poor run having taken three points from their last five games. Bizarrely, Leeds haven’t won a Premier League match that’s kicked off before 3pm since August 2022 – a run of 21 matches.Prediction: Leeds 1-1 Tottenham

Arsenal v Hull (3pm)Arsenal can go six points clear of City at the Premier League summit – for a few hours at least – with a win over Hull. The Gunners have bounced back nicely from their defeat at Brighton with four straight league wins and they seem destined to retain the title they claimed last season. Hull are in freefall having not won since August. This is a home banker.Prediction: Arsenal 3-0 Hull

Fulham v Newcastle (3pm)The pressure on Matthias Jaissle intensified following Newcastle’s limp display against Everton on MNF. The home side were booed off by the St James’ Park faithful and another defeat at Craven Cottage would mean Jaissle will be looking over his shoulder during the international break. If he needs any inspiration, he can take it from Alvaro Arbeloa. The Spaniard was in a similar situation a month ago but seven points from a possible nine has seen the Cottagers move up to 15th.Prediction: Fulham 2-0 Newcastle

Nottingham Forest v Manchester City (5.30pm)The situation is also locking bleak for Oliver Glasner. His move to the City Ground has failed to inspire Nottingham Forest and club chief Evangelos Marinakis is not known for his patience. Forest have performed better than their results suggest but there is no doubt Glasner needs to start winning games, and quickly. He is, therefore, unfortunate to come up against Manchester City this weekend. City have lost their last two Premier League games and have not lost three in a row since 2016. It is unlikely to happen here…Prediction: Nottingham Forest 1-2 Manchester City

Premier League 2026

England

SUNDAY

Brighton v Brentford (2pm)Brighton’s win at Manchester City last Saturday has prompted talk of a title challenge from Fabian Hurzeler’s men. While that may be a touch unrealistic, there is no doubt the Seagulls are set to hang around the upper end of the table for some time. Brentford’s win over Forest last weekend was much needed after a run of four games without a victory in all competitions. These two sides play good football but Brighton’s form means they go in as favourites.Prediction: Brighton 3-1 Brentford

Crystal Palace v Liverpool (2pm)Liverpool head to Selhurst Park having suffered back-to-back defeats for the first time this season – against Arsenal in the league and Fenerbahce in the Champions League. Andoni Iraola is seemingly still trying to work lout his best XI and the Merseysiders have yet to hit top gear. They will never have a better chance of achieving that than against a Palace side that look bereft. Pierre Sage has proved an underwhelming replacement for Glasner and appears a dead man walking.Prediction: Crystal Palace 0-2 Liverpool

Ipswich v Bournemouth (2pm)Thursday’s Europa League win at Sparta Prague means Bournemouth have now won their last seven games in all competitions. It is a remarkable turnaround after a slow start and they will head to Suffolk brimming with confidence. Ipswich will be pleased with their start following promotion and they sit 14th after successive draws with Forest and Hull. Portman Road is not an easy place to win but it’s impossible to go against the Cherries at the minute.Prediction: Ipswich 1-3 Bournemouth

Sunderland v Chelsea (2pm)Sunderland have been a tough watch in recent weeks. Regis Le Bris’ side have developed a nasty habit of missing chances at one end and giving away sloppy goals at the other. That is not a combination that works and the Frenchman needs to restore the physical approach that worked so well last season. Sunderland beat Chelsea in May but this is a different Blues outfit under Xabi Alonso. They still veer from the sublime to the ridiculous but they will fancy their chances of adding to Sunderland’s misery.Prediction: Sunderland 1-1 Chelsea

Manchester United v Aston Villa (4.30pm)Did United’s win over Roma offer Michael Carrick a stay of execution or will the Villa game be his final appearance in the Old Trafford dugout? Only time will tell but there is no doubt the former England midfielder needs a victory in this one to stand any chance of retaining his job. Unai Emery has no such worries and appears to be building another strong side at Villa despite a summer of churn. The visitors look a well-oiled outfit and they may be too much for United.Prediction: Manchester United 1-2 Aston Villa

articles.title: Carrick dismisses comparisons with Ferguson as Manchester United celebrate anniversary of legend’s appointment
articles.summary: Manchester United host Aston Villa on Sunday in another big game for boss Michael Carrick
articles.content:
Carrick dismisses comparisons with Ferguson as Manchester United celebrate anniversary of legend’s appointment

Manchester United host Aston Villa on Sunday in another big game for boss Michael Carrick

Last Update:

Michael Carrick brushed off comparisons with Sir Alex Ferguson and claimed it was important to “live in the present” as he tries to revive Manchester United’s season.

On the 40th anniversary of Ferguson’s appointment, Carrick was reminded of the difficult start to the Scotsman’s time at Old Trafford before he went on to achieve extraordinary success by guiding United to 13 Premier League titles and two Champions League crowns.

Ferguson was on the brink of the sack in 1990 only for an FA Cup win at Nottingham Forest – courtesy of a goal from Mark Robins – to save him and from there the rest is history.

Carrick went into Tuesday night’s Champions League game with Rome in equal peril and stood on the precipice with his team 2-0 down at half-time. However, a second-half comeback that resulted in a 3-2 win has changed the mood ahead of Sunday’s clash with Aston Villa.

Asked about Ferguson today, Carrick said: “More comparisons. You always find something to compare! It is up to us to take it forward. It was a fantastic night [against Roma].

“It was a one-off night. We scored some goals from nowhere. I thought we played really well and deserved to win the game. Nothing is done yet. Nothing is achieved yet. It is one moment in time that we need to use to move forward. We need more of it, for sure.”

Football has changed, says Carrick, when asked about United’s patience with Fergie

Carrick is not convinced he would get the same time today that Ferguson got in 1990.

He added: ”The game has certainly changed, no doubt. It has evolved. It changes, and we have got to deal with what is in front of us. The comparison, I get and I understand. We have got to live in the present. We’re all desperate to win football matches and win them as quickly as we can.”

United are mired in their worst start to a league season since 1986/87, a run that ironically resulted in the dismissal of Ron Atkinson and Ferguson being appointed.

Carrick is confident, though, that his team, who sit one place outside the relegation zone. are moving in the right direction.

“When you watch the [Roma] game back, in the first half it wasn’t so bad. There were moments in there that we left ourselves short really,” he said.

“They’re the moments we have got to clean up on. Little moments here and there that have changed games for us, which is football, something we have to manage – the first half against Chelsea was very good.

“I think we are showing signs of improvement in that respect. We have got to take that moving forward.”

United midfielder Baleba out for several weeks

There was mixed news on the injury front with summer signing Carlos Baleba expected to miss several weeks but left-back Patrick Dorgu close to a return.

Carrick said of the Cameroon midfielder: “Carlos, we don’t know exactly, but it will be a number of weeks. It won’t be any time over the international break. It will be a bit longer than that.

“Patrick has done a little bit of training this week. Very, very small. We have got to be patient with Pat.

“He has had a good period of time now, a couple of hamstrings that we have to manage and be patient with that over the next couple of weeks.

“He is slowly getting back with us, so we will have to see if he can be involved with us at the weekend or not.”

United’s game with Villa kicks off at 4.30pm on Sunday afternoon.

articles.title: Thomas Tuchel takes aim at Cole Palmer and says he wants players to show it ‘matters’ to play for England
articles.summary: Cole Palmer was left out of the England squad named this morning by Thomas Tuchel
articles.content:
Thomas Tuchel takes aim at Cole Palmer and says he wants players to show it ‘matters’ to play for England

Cole Palmer was left out of the England squad named this morning by Thomas Tuchel

Last Update:

Thomas Tuchel insists his refusal to select Cole Palmer in his England squad is nothing personal but says he will always prioritise players who show that playing for the Three Lions “matters”.

Palmer was the headline omission from the group named this morning for the Nations League games with Croatia and Spain and has seemingly paid the price for withdrawing from the last camp with a minor injury.

Tuchel repeated his claim that the Chelsea playmaker “misses too many opportunities to impress” and he will remain on the sidelines for now.

The German said: “I guess everyone is desperate to play for England and Cole is no exception. We are speaking now about a player that is not in camp. It counts when you are in camp and I just said last time that he misses too many opportunities to impress. It was a long camp, it was two and a half weeks and the players and the boys who were in camp built something extraordinary.

“That’s why the credit goes to them, the trust is for them. If you are in camp, this is your chance to impress.

“So it’s not personal and of course we will never assume that Cole is not in the mindset to come and desperate to play for his country, but the competition is on and the players who were in camp did an amazing job and kept their place.”

Tuchel made squad unity a major priority in his World Cup selection – with Palmer excluded – and has remained faithful to that idea.

He added: ”It is always about the ones who are in camp, who don’t withdraw, come to camp and show that it matters.

“I think that [message] is naturally coming through. That was always the message very, very early that is matters if you are in camp.

“The last camp was an excellent one and the trust and belief is in the players who were there.”

England squad in new phase, says Tuchel

England’s World Cup challenge ended at the semi-final stage with question marks around certain inclusions, most notably Dan Burn and Jordan Henderson, who appeared to be included on the basis of their character rather than ability.

But Tuchel says the squad is now entering a new phase.

“I think we did it naturally,” he said. “We were a little bit forced. I was a bit concerned before the last camp because we missed Dean Henderson, John Stones, Dan Burn, Jordan Henderson, Reece James – players who were really responsible for the attitude and the energy at the World Cup and played a huge part in the standards throughout the camp.

“I was a bit worried that we missed so many of them but the group found a new way. They found new leadership, a new way to engage with each other. We built another camp with a good atmosphere, new voices to set the standards.

“Now we have more choices and I had to give Dan Burn, Jordan Henderson, Dean Henderson difficult phone calls. I am very aware of what they did for us and they built a very strong foundation on which these players now are benefitting from.

“Naturally, we went forward. But we always want to go forward and embrace change as something positive. It does not mean the door is closed for these kinds of players. But we decided to give this group kind of a second push.”

Bellingham and King earn England chance

The chief beneficiaries of the change were Jobe Bellingham and Josh King, who both received their first call-ups.

Bellingham joins brother Jude in the squad after a strong start to the season with Borussia Dortmund.

“It’s an incredible achievement for the brothers and the family to be both nominated for the national team, which is an incredible story in itself,” said Tuchel. “I was very happy to give him the call-up and I saw his excitement straight away in his smile. He is a very open and calm personality so it was a very nice phone call, of course, because it was very good news.

“He is one of five players for the central midfield. He is a more defensive player than his brother Jude. Good on the ball, good physique, very physical player who can keep possession. Now it is up to him to impress.”

On Fulham midfielder King, he added: “He is just a fantastic character. He gives us a bit of flexibility.

“We decided to nominate 22 outfield players for flexibility in training and he is the extra player in training, if you will.

“He is an exciting player, a versatile player. In pre-season he helped us in training as a full back but we will not do that again.”

Croatia visit Wembley next Thursday before England head to Madrid the following Sunday. Tuchel’s men sit in second place in Group C and know that if they avoid defeat against Croatia then that will be enough to secure their quarter-final place. To finish top of the group, England would need to win both games and ensure they have a higher goal difference than Spain.

England squad in full

Goalkeepers: Jordan Pickford (Everton), Jason Steele (Brighton & Hove Albion), James Trafford (Leeds United)

Defenders: Trent Alexander-Arnold (Real Madrid), Jarrad Branthwaite (Everton), Marc Guéhi (Manchester City), Lewis Hall (Newcastle United), Ezri Konsa (Arsenal), Jarell Quansah (Bayer Leverkusen), Djed Spence (Inter Milan), Ben White (Arsenal)

Forwards: Dominic Calvert-Lewin (Leeds United), Eberechi Eze (Arsenal), Morgan Gibbs-White (Nottingham Forest), Anthony Gordon (Barcelona), Harry Kane (Bayern Munich), Rio Ngumoha (Liverpool), Morgan Rogers (Chelsea)

articles.content:
BREAKING: Jobe Bellingham receives England call-up alongside his brother Jude

There will be two Bellinghams in the England squad after Jobe's call-up for the games with Croatia and Spain

Last Update:

Borussia Dortmund midfielder Jobe Bellingham was today called into the England squad alongside his brother Jude.

Bellingham has performed well for Dortmund this season with Niko Kovac’s side second in the Bundesliga, trailing Bayern Munich on goal difference only.

The 21-year-old moved to Germany, following the same career path as his older brother, from Sunderland in 2025 after helping the Black Cats to promotion to the Premier League.

Josh King also received a first call-up after starring for Fulham while Arsenal pair Declan Rice and Ben White returned to the squad.

The headline omissions are that of Cole Palmer and Phil Foden. Palmer withdrew from the last England squad with a frustrated Thomas Tuchel claiming the Chelsea star “misses too many opportunities” to play for his country.

Palmer has won just 14 caps for the Three Lions but continues to shine at club level with three goals and three assists in nine games for Chelsea this season.

Foden has not played for England since March.

England conclude their Nations League campaign with games against Croatia and Spain.

Croatia visit Wembley next Thursday before England head to Madrid the following Sunday. Tuchel’s men sit in second place in Group C and know that if they avoid defeat against Croatia then that will be enough to secure their quarter-final place. To finish top of the group, England would need to win both games and ensure they have a higher goal difference than Spain.

Europa League round-up: AC Milan stunned by Ferencvaros as Celtic edge Besiktas in five-goal thriller

Catch up on all the action from Thursday's Europa League fixtures, including games involving AC Milan, Juventus, Celtic and Bayer Leverkusen.

Last Update:

The Europa League returned on Thursday evening with 17 matches taking place across the continent, including several heavyweight clashes.

AC Milan hosted Ferencvaros, Juventus travelled to AZ Alkmaar and Celtic faced Besiktas in Glasgow, while Bayer Leverkusen took on Marseille and Real Sociedad met Lyon.

Here is how the action unfolded.

AC Milan 0-2 Ferencvaros

Lenny Joseph scored twice in the second half as Ferencvaros stunned AC Milan at San Siro.

Joseph broke the deadlock in the 52nd minute before doubling the visitors’ advantage 14 minutes later, leaving Milan facing another European defeat.

Ferencvaros were reduced to 10 men when Yusuf was sent off in the 77th minute, but the Hungarian side held on for the win.

Real Sociedad 1-1 Lyon

Corentin Tolisso scored a superb second-half equaliser as Lyon came from behind to draw 1-1 with Real Sociedad.

Orri Oskarsson had given the Spanish side the lead in the 28th minute, heading home Ander Barrenetxea’s cross from close range.

However, Tolisso levelled nine minutes after the restart, controlling Tanner Tessmann’s lofted pass on his chest before volleying past Unai Marrero.

Both sides had chances to win it late on, with Lyon goalkeeper Dominik Greif denying Mikel Oyarzabal before Marrero produced an excellent save to keep out Tolisso’s header in the 90th minute.

AZ Alkmaar 1-2 Juventus

Juventus beat AZ Alkmaar 2-1 in the Netherlands, with Teun Koopmeiners and Randal Kolo Muani both finding the net for the Italian side.

The visitors established a two-goal advantage during the first half, leaving AZ with a difficult task after the interval.

The Dutch side managed to pull a goal back, but Juventus held on to take all three points.

Bayer Leverkusen 0-1 Marseille

Amine Gouiri struck late in the second half as Marseille beat Bayer Leverkusen 1-0 at the BayArena.

The two sides went into the interval level after a goalless first half, with neither able to find a breakthrough.

Gouiri eventually broke the deadlock in the closing stages to give Marseille a much-needed European win.

Celtic 3-2 Besiktas

Camilo Duran scored twice, including an 87th-minute winner, as Celtic came from behind to beat Besiktas 3-2 in Glasgow.

Junior Olaitan put the visitors ahead in the 54th minute, converting the rebound after his penalty had been saved, before substitute Callum Osmand equalised with a low strike from the edge of the box.

Duran rounded the goalkeeper to put Celtic ahead in the 79th minute, only for Orkun Kokcu to level with a superb effort from 25 yards six minutes later.

However, Duran struck again with three minutes remaining to give Celtic their first win of the league phase.

articles.title: Pierre Sage warns Crystal Palace that Liverpool are a ‘crazy team’ after Europa League draw
articles.summary: Pierre Sage is expecting another tough test for Crystal Palace after their Europa League draw on Thursday.
articles.content:
Pierre Sage warns Crystal Palace that Liverpool are a ‘crazy team’ after Europa League draw

Pierre Sage is expecting another tough test for Crystal Palace after their Europa League draw on Thursday.

Last Update:

Crystal Palace manager Pierre Sage has warned his players to expect a difficult test against Liverpool this weekend, describing the Reds as a “crazy team.”

The Eagles head into the Premier League clash following their Europa League draw with Hoffenheim, in which they battled back despite Adam Wharton’s red card.

Sage praised his players for refusing to give up but admitted Palace must improve their game management after another match disrupted by disciplinary problems.

Speaking to TNT Sports after the match, Sage admitted Palace could have performed better but highlighted the importance of goalkeeper Dean Henderson’s saves.

“I think it could be better if we score before but I know too that Dean Henderson kept us in the game with his saves,” he said.

“I like the energy of the team and to never give up until the end. This goal came at a good moment. We maybe had a last chance to win the game.”

Palace were forced to reorganise after Wharton was sent off, leaving Sage to adjust his defensive setup.

The Frenchman refused to criticise the referee’s decision but acknowledged the impact of losing such an important player.

“I never comment on the decision of the referee,” he added.

Attention now turns to Liverpool, who arrive at the weekend fixture looking to respond after consecutive defeats.

Sage expects Andoni Iraola’s side to be particularly motivated to get back to winning ways and believes Palace must prepare carefully.

“First of all recovery and we have to build the gameplan because it’s a crazy team with really good players,” he said.

“They lost their two last games. I think they will come with a lot of ambition and we have to deal with that.”

articles.title: Portugal boss Jesus tried to talk Ronaldo out of international retirement
articles.summary: Cristiano Ronaldo has walked away from international football despite Portugal boss Jorge Jesus asking him to stay
articles.content:
Portugal boss Jesus tried to talk Ronaldo out of international retirement

Cristiano Ronaldo has walked away from international football despite Portugal boss Jorge Jesus asking him to stay

Last Update:

Jorge Jesus’ fall-out with Cristiano Ronaldo may have influenced the striker’s decision to retire from international football but the Portugal boss insists he tried to persuade the 41-year-old to change his mind.

Ronaldo announced on Thursday that he had quit the international arena after a glittering career that has seen him establish world records for the number of appearances (234) and goals (146).

He departed on a sour note having walked out on the Portugal squad on the eve of their Nations League game against Denmark in September after claiming Jesus had gone back on his word and left him on the bench for the clash with Norway.

Ronaldo was fined €255 and given a 30-day ban by the Portuguese Football Federation but was still expected to be named in the squad for the upcoming games with Denmark and Wales.

It was all Ronaldo’s decision – Jesus

Jesus said he had spoken to the Al-Nassr striker but was unable to persuade him to reverse his decision.

The Portugal boss told Channel 11: “All this is his decision. We had the opportunity to talk about it. I asked him to continue, to continue with me because I needed him to be next to me, but I have to accept his decision.”

Ronaldo’s announcement has prompted a wave of tributes to a player who helped his country win Euro 2016 and two Nations League crowns.

Jesus added: “He is a world reference, a reference of Portugal, a reference of the National Team, of our people, of our history. He is a player who over the years has given a lot to the National Team. He is a symbol for the Portuguese youth. Most of his fans are young.

“In fact, I had a large image of him put in the auditorium so that his presence is always there for the young people.”

It was not an easy decision, but from the heart – Ronaldo

Ronaldo’s announcement came of the blue and just before Jesus was due to name his next squad.

The former Manchester United and Real Madrid star said in a video posted on Instagram and X: “The day has come back for me to hand back the number 7 shirt of our national team.

“I never felt it belonged to me alone. But for 23 years I had the privilege and the responsibility of wearing it, defending it, and carrying it with me into stadiums all around the world.

“Today, the time has come to pass it on to the future. It was not an easy decision. Because some decisions are not made with the mind alone. They are also made with the heart.

“A journey that began in August 2003 and changed my life forever has come to an end. When I look back at everything with the national team, I don’t just see the matches, goals, records or trophies.

“I see people. I see the Portuguese people living abroad who, for 90 minutes, felt a little closer to home. I see millions of Portuguese people I have never met but who became part of my life. Because at the end of the day, football is so much bigger than a game. Football is about people.”

I made mistakes, admits Ronaldo

He added: “Throughout my entire career with the national team I always pushed myself beyond my limits. I wanted to win, I wanted to be better, I wanted to make history. I always demanded the most of myself. I always wanted more. I always believed we could go further. And I gave everything I had for this shirt.

“There were perfect afternoons and nights. There were victories I will never forget. There were defeats that still hurt to remember.

“I made mistakes. I suffered. There were also moments when I couldn’t give the Portuguese people what they so desperately wanted. But I never gave up. And above all, I never stopped feeling proud to represent Portugal.

“Over the years, I learned a few very simple things: Goals fade. Trophies end up in museums. Records are eventually broken. But there is something that time can never erase: the place we hold in people’s hearts. If I ever made you happy, if one of my goals ever made you embrace someone, forget a worry, or feel proud of your country, then it was all worth it. Because being Portuguese is also about this. We suffer together. We rise together. We believe again.

“Portugal will always need young people who dare to dream. Players who never give up. New generations who believe it is possible to go where no one has gone before. Because a country that keeps creating new heroes is a country that never stops believing in itself.”

articles.title: Jaissle shrugs off pressure and remains confident everyone at Newcastle is pulling in same direction
articles.summary: Newcastle face a crunch clash at Fulham on Saturday afternoon with the pressure building on boss Matthias Jaissle
articles.content:
Jaissle shrugs off pressure and remains confident everyone at Newcastle is pulling in same direction

Newcastle face a crunch clash at Fulham on Saturday afternoon with the pressure building on boss Matthias Jaissle

Last Update:

Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle insists he has the support of the board and the players despite growing pressure from a disgruntled fanbase.

Newcastle were booed off following Monday night’s 1-0 defeat at home to Everton – their second loss to the Toffees in four days following the EFL Cup elimination at the Hill Dickinson Stadium last week.

It was also Newcastle’s fourth defeat in five games, leaving them 13th in the Premier League table.

Jaissle, who was the surprise replacement for Eddie Howe in the summer, takes his side to Fulham at the weekend convinced everyone in the squad is pulling in the same direction.

“Yes, of course,” he said. “That was never in question, at least I am not aware of it. We have such a good group and such a good relationship already that the door is always open and if anything is unclear they are more than welcome to talk about it.

“When you see them in training and see how we are doing, I am pretty sure that everyone understands and are fully committed.

“You don’t see the happiest players but you see players in their face that they want to show a reaction. They are also giving me the feeling that they want to be responsible for that. We addressed that. The players addressed that also within themselves.”

Newcastle players ‘really clear’ over tactics

While the players have sometimes looked baffled by the German’s tactics, Jaissle is confident everyone is clear what is expected of them.

He added: “Really clear. As we lead with open doors, we listen a lot. Not only talking. It is important in my leadership style that you listen to the players and we offer them always an open door so if there is anything unclear then they will drop in when they have the chance.

“It’s like always in life and in football, sometimes you want to do your best but it’s a day where you just couldn’t and that was the case against Everton. We didn’t show a lot of things we wanted to do.”

I get a good feeling from within the club – Jaissle

Asked if he feels any concern over his position at St James’ Park, Jaissle said: “I try to not follow things that are written but here and there you get some comments. The nice part is that I got more of a feeling from within the club about how committed they are and that is something really important in a week where there is speculation or rumours. It was good to know, good to feel but I try again in these aspects not to be distracted.”

There was mixed news on the injury front ahead of the trip to Craven Cottage with Lewis Miley progressing nicely and Matias Fernandez-Pardo ready to return from a virus but veteran midfielder Joelinton is set for another spell on the sidelines.

Jaissle said of the Brazilian: “Joelinton unfortunately went out with an injury again and we need to make the final treatment plan for him and see how long he will be out for.”

Cristiano Ronaldo announces retirement from international football

Cristiano Ronaldo has retired from Portugal duty with immediate effect

Last Update:

Portugal striker Cristiano Ronaldo has retired from international football.

The 41-year-old has opted to walk away following a major falling-out with national team boss Jorge Jesus during the last international break.

Ronaldo left the squad in Copenhagen on the eve of their Nations League clash with Denmark having been left on the bench for the previous game against Norway. He was fined €255 (£215; $286) and given a 30-day ban by the Portuguese Football Federation.

It was expected conciliatory talks would resolve the situation and he would return for the upcoming games with Denmark and Wales but he has decided to quit the international game.

“The day has come back for me to hand back the number 7 shirt of our national team,” he said in a statement on Instagram and X. “I never felt it belonged to me alone. Record-breaking Ronaldo bows out for Portugal

Ronaldo departs having made the most international appearances in history (234) and scored the most goals (146).

He made his international debut in 2003 and led Portugal to the 2016 European Championship as well as two Nations League titles.

He added: “Throughout my entire career with the national team I always pushed myself beyond my limits. I wanted to win, I wanted to be better, I wanted to make history. I always demanded the most of myself. I always wanted more. I always believed we could go further. And I gave everything I had for this shirt.

“Portugal will always need young people who dare to dream. Players who never give up. New generations who believe it is possible to go where no one has gone before. Because a country that keeps creating new heroes is a country that never stops believing in itself.”

Ronaldo’s final appearance for Portugal came against Wales in September.

He will now focus his efforts on club matters with Saudi Pro League side Al-Nassr, with whom he won the title last season.

articles.title: Harry Kane signs record-breaking deal at Bayern Munich and admits “this is the best time of my life”
articles.summary: England captain Harry Kane is living his best life after signing a new, three-year deal with Bayern Munich
articles.content:
Harry Kane signs record-breaking deal at Bayern Munich and admits “this is the best time of my life”

England captain Harry Kane is living his best life after signing a new, three-year deal with Bayern Munich

Last Update:

Harry Kane is currently enjoying “the best time of my life” after signing a lucrative new contract at Bayern Munich.

The deal had been in the pipeline for some time but was announced on Thursday morning with Kane agreeing to stay at the Allianz Arena until 2029.

It caps a wonderful fortnight for the 33-year-old, who last week won the Ballon d’Or in London.

“This is the best time of my life. Last season was too – these are the best moments both on and off the pitch. It’s been quite mad of late – in a good way. Personally, I don’t necessarily need the attention; it’s quite a lot to take in, emotionally and mentally. But it’s a great place to be,” he said.

“I’m not the sort of person who lets it go to my head; there are bound to be some low points just round the corner that I’ll have to deal with. I’m staying focused, and the last year has been incredible. At the moment, I feel really at home – hopefully it’ll stay that way for a long time to come.”

Kane – I always believed in myself

Kane left Tottenham for Bayern in the summer of 2023 and has gone from strength to strength, contributing hugely to the club winning two Bundesliga titles with 156 goals in 161 games.

He added: “When a club like Bayern comes in, it’s exciting. I imagined challenging for the league, the cup and the Champions League every year. But there’s also the pressure to perform – on the pitch and off it, having that connection to the fans and the club.

“It was a big move. I felt comfortable at Tottenham. It’s obviously difficult making such a big move, but I’ve always believed in myself. Wherever I’ve played, I’ve scored goals and helped my team – that’s happened here too. The belief in yourself is an important factor.”

Kane has impressed as much off the field as on it during his time in Bavaria, a point the club’s heirarchy was eager to point out.

Sporting director Max Eberl said: “Harry is a true professional, just as you’d imagine. It’s not just about his outstanding, world-class performances on the pitch, but also about the man who embodies everything football should be.

“He’s a family man. In today’s world, which is so frenzied, to have someone like him – who would have every reason to say he’s something special, yet doesn’t – that’s what makes him extraordinary, both as a footballer and as a person. After the 4-1 defeat in Barcelona at the start of Vincent Kompany’s tenure, Harry stood up and gave a speech. That really impressed me. He’s a role model both on and off the pitch; you don’t need many words – that’s enough.”

Kane deal was ‘worth every cent’ – Bayern CEO

Kane’s renewal is a sign of intent for Bayern, who have reportedly made the England captain the highest-paid player in Europe.

CEO Jan-Christian Dreesen said: “Three years ago, this was our biggest transfer. Harry was worth every cent, though, in every respect. He carries the play, makes his team-mates better and is a role model beyond the sport.

“If we want to remain attractive, to compete at the top in Europe, we have to be financially strong. We want to use every cent we earn to be as good as possible. And when the world’s best player gets a top contract, that’s only logical. We want to be stable and sensible financially, but we also want to have the best team and win. That’s not easy against the financial power of other clubs, but we’re managing it pretty well.”

articles.title: Barcelona forward Raphinha signs new, long-term contract
articles.summary: Barcelona have tied Raphinha down to a new deal at Camp Nou
articles.content:
Barcelona forward Raphinha signs new, long-term contract

Barcelona have tied Raphinha down to a new deal at Camp Nou

Last Update:

Raphinha has signed a contract extension with Barcelona that ties him to the club until 2030.

The Brazil international has been a huge success at Camp Nou after joining from Leeds in 2022. In all, he has made 190 appearances for the Blaugrana, scoring 94 goals and adding 55 assists.

He has been in sparkling form this season with 19 goals and three assists in just 13 games.

I want to end my career with Barcelona – Raphinha

Raphinha, 29, said: “It’s a feeling of great pride on my part and for my family. Only we know what we went through internally. I feel very proud of everything I have conquered, individually and collectively. I hope, if my legs allow me to continue at a high level, to finish my career at the club. I will do everything I can for Barcelona.”

Robert Lewandowski’s departure for Chicago Fire meant Barca went into the season without a recognised number nine with Raphinha deployed in that role, initially as a stop-gap. However, his success means it could become a more permanent arrangement in what is a fluid front-four.

He added: “I am surprised by the numbers. I didn’t expect to get to this point with so many goals. I have changed my position a lot but always trying to do my best for my team-mates and the coach.

“I try to adapt quickly. When they told me to play number nine, I gave everything to adapt. I knew I could score goals, with the quality we have, but the numbers have surprised me a little. Now I think we can go much further.”

Barcelona are in good shape – Raphinha

Barca lead the way in La Liga – despite losing the season’s first El Clasico to arch-rivals Real Madrid – and sit in fifth place in the Champions League table having won three of four games with the only setback coming against Paris Saint-Germain.

Raphinha added: “The team is very good. We are in good shape. There are hard defeats, but this does not change the work. Against PSG we know the strength they have, they are the two-time European champions, and against Madrid anything can happen in a Clasico. Maybe we weren’t so good defensively.

“We have lost three points, but we are still leaders in La Liga and in good shape. I want to win the Champions League, but I also want to win the other three titles we can go for.”

articles.title: Who are the best-paid footballers in Europe?
articles.summary: Harry Kane is now the best-paid footballer in Europe by salary. But who else makes up the list of the best-paid footballers in Europe?
articles.content:
Who are the best-paid footballers in Europe?

Harry Kane is now the best-paid footballer in Europe by salary. But who else makes up the list of the best-paid footballers in Europe?

Last Update:

Harry Kane’s new, three-year deal at Bayern Munich makes him the player with the highest base salary in Europe.

The England captain is now thought to be earning in the region of £500,000 a week before bonuses and endorsements on a contract that runs until 2029.

Kane has scored 156 goals in 161 competitive appearances since moving to Munich from Tottenham, helping the club to two Bundesliga titles and one DFB-Pokal. He was also handed the 2026 Ballon d’Or last month.

He told the club’s official website: “I feel right at home at FC Bayern. I love the club, the fans and the city of Munich. We have a fantastic team and, in Vincent Kompany, a fantastic manager. It makes me very proud to be part of this club. My whole family is very happy here. I was keen to stay. I’m now looking forward to the future and I want to win many more titles with this great club.”

Bayern president Herbert Hainer added: “What began as a major transfer has, over time, become a special chapter in FC Bayern’s history. Harry Kane lives up to every promise football has to offer, and he has secured his place in the hearts of the fans as one of the greatest figures in the sport of our time. My compliments to Jan-Christian Dreesen and our sporting management team. This is a special moment for FC Bayern today.”

Kane, 33, has excelled since leaving the Premier League for the Bundesliga and this new deal reflects his status as one of the best players in the world.

But how does it compare financially to Europe’s other big hitters?

The Top 10 best-paid footballers in Europe

1. Harry Kane (Bayern Munich) – £500,000 a week

The England captain now sits at the top of the tree. At 33, this is likely to be his last bumper pay deal.

2. Kylian Mbappe (Real Madrid) – £495,000 a week

Smaller than Kane’s by salary but, having joined on a free transfer from Paris Saint-Germain in 2024, France captain Mbappe also receives an annual payment in the region of £30million as part of his signing on fee.

3. Erling Haaland (Manchester City) – £480,000 a week

Haaland signed a nine-and-a-half year contract at the Etihad in January 2025 on terms that reflected his status as one of the best strikers in the world. His base may be slightly smaller than Kane’s but his bonuses and endorsements propel him well beyond the former Spurs man.

4. Vinicius Jr (Real Madrid) – £475,000 a week

After months of wrangling, Vinicius Jr and Real Madrid finally came to an agreement that saw the Brazil winger sign a new, six-year deal at the Bernabeu in August. Another who has hugely lucrative endorsements with the likes of Pepsi and Nike.

5. Rodri (Barcelona) – £425,000 a week

Barcelona managed to prise the Spain midfielder out of Manchester City over the summer and his worth to club and country was reflected in a lucrative salary.

6. Jamaal Musiala (Bayern Munich) – £367,000 a week

A slightly surprising inclusion this high up the list but the Bayern star signed his deal in 2025 when he was at the peak of his powers and on his way to becoming one of the most exciting players in Europe. Injuries have stalled the 23-year-old’s progress.

7. Lamine Yamal (Barcelona) – £364,000 a week

Still only 19 years of age, the Barcelona star penned a new deal in May 2025 that is loaded with incentives as he develops. His base is eye-watering already but he has the potential to earn the most of any player on the list when linked to endorsements and future contracts.

8. Virgil van Dijk (Liverpool) – £350,000 a week

The Liverpool captain signed a new deal at Anfield in April 2025 and continues to play at the highest level at the age of 35. Has arguably been the best central defender in world football over the duration of his time on Merseyside.

9. Trent Alexander-Arnold (Real Madrid) – £340,000 a week

Having agreed to join Real Madrid on a free after letting his Liverpool contract wind down, the Spanish club were ultimately forced to pay a small fee to enable him to play in the 2025 FIFA Club World Cup. His time at the Bernabeu has not gone as planned.

10. Enzo Fernandez (Manchester City) – £325,000 a week

The Argentina star joined City from Chelsea over the summer as part of a midfield rebuild that also included the arrival of Elliot Anderson. Has been transferred twice for over £100m and his salary reflects that.

articles.title: Como make Champions League history with remarkable Lens rout
articles.summary: Cesc Fabregas' men became only the second team to score nine in a Champions League game.
articles.content:
Como make Champions League history with remarkable Lens rout

Cesc Fabregas' men became only the second team to score nine in a Champions League game.

Last Update:

Como equalled the biggest win in Champions League history as they thrashed Lens by an incredible 9-1 scoreline.

The Serie A club tied the 8-0 wins recorded by Liverpool (v Besiktas in 2007) and Real Madrid (v Malmo in 2015) as they became only the second team to score nine goals in a Champions League game, emulating Bayern Munich, who beat Dinamo Zagreb 9-2 on the opening night of the 2024-25 league phase.

Como beat Manchester United 4-1 in their previous encounter, with coach Cesc Fabregas joking afterwards that he told his players to slow down at 4-0.

There was no slowing down in Northern France, where Tasos Douvikas opened the scoring in the seventh minute with a close-range finish.

Douvikas doubled the lead just after the half-hour mark, before Nico Paz fired into the roof of the net to make it 3-0.

Lucas Da Cunha rifled into the bottom-left corner to score the first of six second-half goals, with Marc-Oliver Kempf then heading in Como’s fifth.

Paz played in Douvikas to complete his hat-trick before Mattia Liberali squeaked home a seventh at the near post.

Ruben Aguilar gave Lens something to cheer with a fine strike from Florian Thauvin’s corner, but normal service was resumed as intricate build-up between Liberali and Martin Baturina saw the latter make it 8-1.

And history was made as Matteo Papaccioli rounded off a historic rout, the debutant’s effort awarded by VAR after initially being ruled out for offside.

Porto put Napoli to the sword

Porto were less emphatic winners, but their 4-1 victory over Napoli represented one of the most impressive performances of the night.

Jan Bednarek headed Porto in front but, after Kevin De Bruyne had an equaliser ruled out for offside, Scott McTominay levelled shortly before half-time.

Gabriel Veiga restored Porto’s advantage when he fired a 71st-minute effort through the legs of Alex Meret, who was helpless as Jakub Kiwior was left unmarked to head home a third for the hosts. The points were then sealed as Samu converted from the penalty spot after being hauled down by Rafa Marin, who was sent off.

Borussia Dortmund ended Real Betis’ unbeaten start to the league phase with a 2-1 win at Signal Iduna Park, Konstantinos Karetsas scoring the winning goal for the Bundesliga side.

Club Brugge made it a third straight Champions League win by prevailing 2-1 away at PSV Eindhoven, while Viking claimed their first win in the competition by seeing off Sabah 4-1.

articles.content:
BREAKING: Tennis legend Nadal joins Real Madrid’s board of directors

Last Update:

Real Madrid have announced that 14-time French Open champion Rafael Nadal has joined the club’s board of directors.

Nadal is a lifelong Madrid fan despite being born and brought up in Mallorca.

The Spaniard retired in November 2024 after a glittering career that saw him win 22 grand slam crowns in total – including his record haul at Roland Garros – to sit second on the all-time list behind Novak Djokovic.

Alongside his tennis academy in Mallorca, Nadal is known to be eager to build his business interests and he will now have a say in the future of Real Madrid.

A club statement on Wednesday read: “The Board of Directors of Real Madrid CF, meeting today, Wednesday, November 4, has agreed to submit to the General Assembly of Compromise Partners the ratification of the appointment of Rafael Nadal Parera, member number 67,778 of our club, as a new member of the Board of Directors.

“Rafael Nadal, honorary member of Real Madrid, is one of the greatest legends in the history of sports and one of the most admired and recognized Spanish athletes worldwide.

“For Real Madrid, it is a huge pride that a figure of his sporting and human dimension, a reference of Spanish and world sport, becomes part of our Board of Directors and contributes, from this responsibility, to the present and future of our club.”

Real Madrid – Nadal shares the club’s values

The statement continued: “With his extraordinary track record, with 92 individual titles, including 22 grand slams, two Olympic gold medals, five Davis Cups with Spain and the number one in the world ranking, Rafael Nadal has starred in a legendary sporting career. But his stature represents much more than his successes: his talent, his spirit of permanent improvement, his capacity for sacrifice, his competitiveness, his humility, his respect for rivals and his team-mates, and his commitment to solidarity make him an example on and off the court.

“All these values are part of the identity of Real Madrid and Rafael Nadal has represented and defended them throughout his sporting life, becoming a benchmark for millions of people around the world.”

Nadal was thrilled by the news, saying: ” want to thank president Florentino Pérez and the Board for proposing that I join the Board of Directors of @realmadrid. I have accepted this proposal with great excitement, a desire to learn, and a willingness to contribute everything I can.”

articles.title: Parker excited to return to West Ham and receive ‘warmth and love’
articles.summary: Scott Parker was this morning named the new head coach of West Ham
articles.content:
Parker excited to return to West Ham and receive ‘warmth and love’

Scott Parker was this morning named the new head coach of West Ham

Last Update:

Scott Parker is hoping to replicate the “warmth and love” he enjoyed as a player at West Ham after being appointed the club’s new head coach on Wednesday.

Parker succeeds Nuno Espirito Santo, who was sacked yesterday with the Hammers eighth in the Championship table and having suffered successive home defeats to promotion rivals Southampton and West Brom.

The 46-year-old has signed a two-and-a-half-year contract at the London Stadium and will be in the dugout for tonight’s game at Cardiff.

It is an emotional return to the capital for Parker, who made 129 appearances for West Ham as a player and was named Hammer of the Year three times as well as winning the Football Writers’ Association Footballer of the Year award in the 2010/11 season.

He told the club’s official website: “It is a very proud moment for me to step into this role and return to a club that means so much to me and my family. A lot of very fond memories of my time here – four years of probably the best football I played in my career.

“There was a warmth, a love, a feeling that I probably didn’t have anywhere else. There was something which stood out constantly and that was the relationship that I built up with the fanbase here. That rapport and respect, that I felt instantly.

“More than anything, this is an opportunity that I am very excited about. I feel privileged and honoured to be the guy that wants to lead us back to the Premier League and be the head coach of this football club at this moment in time.

“My energy levels, my enthusiasm, my desire, my passion – it’s absolutely running through and that’s the feeling I had as soon as there was a conversation that this was possible. That’s exactly why I’m here and why I want to be here.”

Parker aiming for fourth Championship promotion with West Ham

Parker has experience of getting out of the Championship having achieved it with Fulham, Bournemouth and Burnley. He added: “I’ve been in this division three times and I’ve got out of this division three times. This is a tough division, there is absolutely no denying it. And I will use every ounce of my experience, every ounce of my knowledge, to have an understanding of what we’re going to need to bring consistency.

“And that’s going to be the key word for all of us really. The consistency of what we do and the commitment levels that we go to will give us the best opportunity to get out of this division and be the team that we can be.”

West Ham United interim CEO Karim Virani added: “We are delighted to welcome Scott and his family back to the club. He is someone who is held in high regard at West Ham United and throughout the game, and he was the unanimous choice of the board to become our new head coach.

“He has fantastic experience and pedigree across an outstanding playing and coaching career, a clear and proven track record of success as a head coach in the EFL Championship, and a deep understanding of West Ham United, its identity and our loyal and passionate fanbase.

“We believe that all of these factors together make him the right man to lead us forward and help the club to achieve our objectives this season and beyond. Scott has the complete support of everyone here and, from the conversations we have had with him already, we believe he will represent West Ham United and our supporters in a way that we can all be extremely proud of.”

articles.title: Owono ‘would never intentionally harm anyone’, says Andorra team-mate following De Miguel death
articles.summary: Jesus Owono is suffering following his role in the death of Tenerife forward Jesús de Miguel, according to FC Andorra team-mate Lautaro Spatz
articles.content:
Owono ‘would never intentionally harm anyone’, says Andorra team-mate following De Miguel death

Jesus Owono is suffering following his role in the death of Tenerife forward Jesús de Miguel, according to FC Andorra team-mate Lautaro Spatz

Last Update:

FC Andorra defender Lautaro Spatz has leapt to the defence of goalkeeper Jesus Owono following the collision that killed Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel.

Owono came racing out of his goal and clattered into De Miguel during Monday’s Segunda Division game at the Estadio Heliodoro Rodríguez López in Santa Cruz.

There was immediate concern for the 30-year-old as he lay stricken on the turf with players from both sides, including Owono who was quick to check on De Miguel after being sent-off, rushing to his aid.

He was taken to hospital but, despite positive initial updates, it was announced on Tuesday morning that he had passed away.

Owono criticism is unfair, says Spatz

Amid the grief, there has been widespread criticism of Equatorial Guinea international Owono for the reckless nature of the challenge.

But Spatz says that is unfair and revealed the 25-year-old has been “profoundly affected” by the incident.

Writing on Instagram, Argentine Spatz said: “There are moments when soccer stops making sense.

“Moments that stay with you forever and make you realise just how fragile life can be. What we experienced is something none of us will ever forget. A tragedy that has left us completely devastated, speechless, and struggling to put our sadness into words.

“First and foremost, I want to express my deepest condolences and all my love to Jesús’ family, friends, and loved ones. I also want to extend those thoughts to the entire Tenerife family and the wider soccer community. Since yesterday, everyone in the FC Andorra squad has been shocked, heartbroken, and deeply affected by what happened. It is a tragedy we never could have imagined experiencing on a soccer field.

“I also want to say a few words about my team-mate, goalkeeper, and friend, who has been profoundly affected by what happened. Those of us who know him understand the kind of person he is, how much he is suffering right now, and that he would never intentionally harm anyone.

“In soccer, freak incidents can happen, but no one could ever imagine one ending with such tragic consequences. Today, soccer doesn’t matter. All that remains is to stand together in grief, show the utmost respect, and send all our strength to the family and everyone suffering through this terrible loss. Rest in peace.”

Spanish police have opened an investigation into possible involuntary manslaughter against Owono.

articles.title: Mikel Arteta hits back at Liverpool penalty complaints: ‘I have a massive library’
articles.summary: Mikel Arteta dismisses Liverpool's penalty complaints after Arsenal's 1-0 win at Anfield, claiming he has a "massive library" of similar incidents.
articles.content:
Mikel Arteta hits back at Liverpool penalty complaints: ‘I have a massive library’

Mikel Arteta dismisses Liverpool's penalty complaints after Arsenal's 1-0 win at Anfield, claiming he has a "massive library" of similar incidents.

Last Update:

Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta has dismissed Liverpool’s complaints over a controversial penalty decision during Sunday’s 1-0 win at Anfield, insisting he has a “massive library” of similar incidents that have gone unpunished.

The Gunners secured their first league win at Anfield since 2012, moving three points clear at the top of the Premier League in the process.

However, Liverpool were left furious after Jurrien Timber escaped punishment for pulling Alexander Isak’s shirt inside the penalty area.

Reds boss Andoni Iraola criticised the decision after the match, suggesting he would encourage his players to go to ground in similar situations in future.

Speaking ahead of Arsenal’s Champions League clash with Slavia Prague, Arteta was asked about the incident involving Timber and Isak.

The Spaniard had initially claimed he had not seen a replay immediately after Sunday’s match but was unwilling to entertain suggestions that Arsenal had benefited from a fortunate decision.

“I have a lot of clips about shirts, pulls, grabs,” Arteta said.

“I have a massive library that we can talk about. We’re talking about one in particular, I have a massive library that we can throw there to remind everybody what every team is going through.”

Arsenal boss has previously criticised refereeing consistency

It is not the first time Arteta has spoken about keeping evidence of incidents he believes highlight inconsistencies in officiating.

Last month, the Arsenal manager revealed he had been collecting footage of other Premier League coaches leaving their technical areas without receiving yellow cards.

Arteta has already been booked against Sunderland and Leeds this season, meaning another caution would result in a touchline suspension.

“There are managers who have the record in the league, 36 times in 10 minutes [they] leave the touchline – no yellows,” he said at the time.

“I am clipping all of that so I have now a massive storage of images, so if somebody comes to me I can say, ‘I am not in the record yet’.

“Somebody else has the record so let’s see.

“Then it’s 36 yellow cards in 10 minutes for the managers. I don’t know what we are going to do – let’s see.”

articles.title: Jose Mourinho claims he needs ‘three years’ to reach perfection at Real Madrid
articles.summary: Jose Mourinho claims he needs three years to achieve perfection at Real Madrid.
articles.content:
Jose Mourinho claims he needs ‘three years’ to reach perfection at Real Madrid

Jose Mourinho claims he needs three years to achieve perfection at Real Madrid.

Last Update:

Real Madrid manager Jose Mourinho believes it will take three years to get his side playing at their best.

The Portuguese coach, who signed a three-year contract in the summer, was asked how long it would take to achieve perfection at the Santiago Bernabeu.

“Three years. Three seasons,” Mourinho replied.

His comments came ahead of Wednesday’s Champions League trip to AEK Athens, and he was also quizzed on his attacking options, with Vinicius Junior, Kylian Mbappe and Yan Diomande among those competing for places.

“You are also forgetting Brahim and Endrick. We have a lot of quality players here. For me, having a large number of players is never a problem,” he said.

The Madrid boss identified Vinicius as his most natural option on the left wing but stressed that several players could operate across different attacking positions.

Attention then turned to Wednesday’s trip to Greece, where Mourinho warned against underestimating AEK Athens.

“Greece is always difficult, and Real Madrid, the king of Europe, has achieved only one win in eight visits to Greece,” he explained.

“Every opponent that sees the white shirt in front of them is highly motivated.”

Mourinho added: “It is a match in which we must be at the peak of our concentration and readiness, and if we are not, we will not win.”

articles.title: ‘I don’t have time’ – Andoni Iraola dismisses Arsenal controversy as Liverpool prepare for Champions League clash
articles.summary: Andoni Iraola refuses to dwell on refereeing decisions against Arsenal as Liverpool prepare for a Champions League trip to Istanbul.
articles.content:
‘I don’t have time’ – Andoni Iraola dismisses Arsenal controversy as Liverpool prepare for Champions League clash

Andoni Iraola refuses to dwell on refereeing decisions against Arsenal as Liverpool prepare for a Champions League trip to Istanbul.

Last Update:

Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola has refused to dwell on controversial refereeing decisions against Arsenal, insisting his focus is firmly on the Champions League ahead of his side’s trip to Istanbul.

The Reds are looking to bounce back from their Premier League defeat to the Gunners and maintain their perfect record in Europe, having collected nine points from their opening three Champions League matches.

Iraola believes there were plenty of positives to take from the Arsenal performance but has urged his players to improve their movement in the opposition penalty area.

Speaking ahead of Liverpool’s Champions League fixture, Iraola was asked whether he had sought clarification from PGMOL over decisions made during the defeat to Arsenal.

“I didn’t ask for an explanation. I told you what I think about the plays but honestly I don’t have time,” he said.

“Been preparing for this game, focusing on the opposition and how to prepare the team for tomorrow.

“It is difficult when you lose but I am happy with a lot of things from the other day,” he explained.

“Still we need to improve, especially attacking in the box. A lot of times we had the numbers there but not making the proper runs.

“We put Arsenal under pressure, they defended well but I liked a lot of things.”

Liverpool boss targets fourth straight Champions League win in Istanbul

Liverpool return to Istanbul, the city where they famously overturned a three-goal deficit against AC Milan to win the 2005 Champions League final.

Iraola acknowledged the significance of the city to Liverpool’s history but warned that his players face a difficult European assignment.

“Istanbul is always going to be very special for Liverpool. It is difficult to find a more important night,” he said.

“Tomorrow it won’t be easy, you talk about statistics, especially English teams playing here. They have very good players and a very good squad, they know how to play in this competition. We have to start strong in the game.

“We want to continue how we have done in the Champions League, three games and nine points, it is a good chance to get to 12 points and then finish in the top eight,” Iraola added.

“Champions League away is very difficult.”

articles.title: Lionel Messi and Kylian Mbappe lead tributes to Jesus de Miguel after tragic death
articles.summary: The world of football is in mourning following the death of Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel
articles.content:
Lionel Messi and Kylian Mbappe lead tributes to Jesus de Miguel after tragic death

The world of football is in mourning following the death of Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel

Last Update:

Lionel Messi and Kylian Mbappe have led the tributes to Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel who died this morning after sustaining serious injuries in Monday’s Segunda Division game with Andorra.

The 30-year-old collided with visiting goalkeeper Jesus Owono when chasing a long ball and there was immediate concern from players and medical staff.

The game was abandoned and De Miguel taken to hospital. An early update said the player was “serious but stable” but his condition deteriorated and his passing was announced this morning.

The news has devastated the football community in Spain and around the world with tributes flowing in for a player who also represented Navalcarnero, Unionistas and Castellon among others.

Inter Miami star Messi, who spent the bulk of his carer at Barcelona, wrote on Instagram: “There are no words… My condolences and much strength to all his family and friends. RIP

Pedri and Mbappe pay tribute to De Miguel

Barcelona midfielder Pedri, who was born and brought up in Tenerife, said: “The death of Jesús de Miguel leaves me speechless. A huge hug for his family and one to CD Tenerife. Rest in peace.”

That sentiment was also shared by Real Madrid star Mbappe. The France captain wrote on Instagram: “A lot of sadness, there are no words.”

In addition to the many social media messages were more formal notes of condolence.

The Real Madrid squad paused for a minute’s silence before training today with a club communique reading: “Real Madrid CF, its president, and its Board of Directors deeply regret the passing of Jesús de Miguel, player of CD Tenerife.

“Real Madrid wishes to express its condolences and affection to his family, his team-mates, his club, and all his loved ones.”

Barcelona said: “From FC Barcelona, we deeply regret the tragic news of the passing of CD Tenerife player Jesús de Miguel. Our thoughts and support are with his family, friends and loved ones during these difficult times.”

The Spanish Football Federation suspended all activity on Tuesday, and later announced there would be no games staged until November 6.

A statement on X read: “In a sign of respect and solidarity following the passing of Jesús de Miguel, the RFEF has agreed to extend the suspension of its competitions until November 6.

“The Copa del Rey and Copa de la Reina matches scheduled for this week are therefore postponed.

“The entire Spanish football family stands united in grief following this tragic loss and extends its deepest condolences, love and support to the family, friends and loved ones of Jesús de Miguel, as well as to everyone at CD Tenerife and its supporters during these extremely difficult times.”

Tenerife announce De Miguel’s passing

The news that De Miguel had passed away was conveyed this morning in a statement from Tenerife.

It read: “Racked with pain, with a lump in our throats and unable to believe that this is true, CD Tenerife communicates the tragic passing, this Tuesday, November 3, 2026, at 8:00 a.m., of Jesús de Miguel Alameda.

“There are no words of comfort; there is absolutely nothing that can alleviate this feeling overflowing with sadness. We stand alongside his devastated family, alongside his loved ones, alongside all of tinerfeñismo that today weeps for this cruel outcome.

“The family of Jesús de Miguel thanks each and every one of the expressions of support received, and likewise requests, from the heart, the utmost respect for their privacy in these terrible moments.”

Owono was red-carded for the challenge but any anger was quickly put to one side with players rushing to De Miguel’s aid.

An Andorra statement read: “With broken hearts and devastation, we want to send our most sincere condolences to the family of Jesús de Miguel, to all his team-mates, friends, and to CD Tenerife. Rest in peace.”

Spanish police have opened an investigation into possible involuntary manslaughter against Owono.
