articles.title: Real Madrid apologise for Mbappe gaffe and express ‘deep respect for China’
articles.summary: Real Madrid have apologised to the Chinese people following Kylian Mbappe's remarks about the country's former leader Mao Zedong
articles.content:
Real Madrid apologise for Mbappe gaffe and express ‘deep respect for China’

Real Madrid have apologised to the Chinese people following Kylian Mbappe's remarks about the country's former leader Mao Zedong

Last Update:

Real Madrid have issued an official apology to the Chinese people as the row over Kylian Mbappe’s ill-judged remarks regarding Mao Zedong shows no sign of abating.

Mbappe said sorry on Tuesday after suggesting he found a meme that superimposed his face on to “some guy – I think he’s a Chinese dictator” funny. The meme in question featured Mao, the country’s founding leader who died in 1976. Mao’s policies are widely blamed for mass starvation and millions of deaths but it is still taboo in China to mock a historical figure of his prominence.

There have been reports Chinese state television have suspended broadcasts of La Liga matches in protest and Real Madrid moved on Wednesday to offer their apologies.

A club statement read: “Real Madrid wishes to express its apologies to the Chinese people for any discomfort that may have been caused by the recent words of our player Kylian Mbappé.

“Our club holds deep respect for China, its history, its culture, and its citizens, as well as for the millions of Chinese fans who feel affection and admiration for Real Madrid.

“The club joins the public apology expressed by Kylian Mbappé, in which the player himself has conveyed his regret for his words and reiterated his respect for the Chinese people.

“Real Madrid reaffirms its commitment to the values of respect, coexistence, and understanding among cultures, and expresses its desire to continue strengthening the bonds of friendship and affection that unite it with China and its citizens.”

Kylian Mbappe: Full apology to people in China

Mbappe, who made the remarks on YouTube show The Bridge hosted by Blancos team-mate Aurelien Tchouameni, showed remorse for his words on Tuesday.

“During a recent interview, I reacted to an image featuring myself,” said Mbappe. “My comment was ill-judged and I now understand that it hurt many people in China and in Chinese communities around the world.

“I apologise to everyone my words have upset. That was absolutely not my intention. I have deep respect for the Chinese people and their history and I am sincerely sorry.”

What is Kylian Mbappe alleged to have said about China?

In unverified clips online, Mbappe does not name Mao but says he uses the meme “all the time” with friends, adding that it “makes me laugh the most… there’s a video of a guy, I think it’s a Chinese dictator…”

Chinese football forum Dongqiudi reportedly highlighted the interview, calling it “inappropriate” and liable to “hurt the feelings of Chinese people”.

Mao is an icon of the Communist Party in China, where the internet and digital content are subject to strict state control and the former leader is one of the most closely regulated topics.

The original video is not on The Bridge’s YouTube channel and it is unclear when the episode first aired. Mbappe spoke in September about memes depicting him as a dictator, which is his apparent nickname in the Madrid dressing room. “Part of it is funny because you get the sense that, for some people, it’s all in good fun,” he told L’Equipe.

“There’s also a less funny part because we know the damage these kinds of people have caused throughout history.

“To be compared to people who murder others, or who have made millions and millions of people unhappy… I don’t think I’ve ever done anything like that in my life.

“So there’s a mix of things. On the one hand, I know it’s done in a light-hearted way and doesn’t go that far, but it sometimes shows a lack of political and human awareness in people.”

Kylian Mbappe: Full La Liga statement

La Liga said it “deeply regrets the offence caused” to Chinese fans. “These comments were made in a personal capacity and do not represent La Liga,” it added.

“To the extent of our institutional responsibility, we apologize on behalf of La Liga and all its clubs.

“Spanish football upholds respect, coexistence, and unity among people of all cultures. We convey our respect to China, its institutions and its people and we deeply value the support of the millions of fans who follow us each week.

“We reaffirm our commitment to a relationship built over years. We are working with our partners and institutional interlocutors in China to address this situation.

“Likewise, in collaboration with the clubs and players, we will implement a protocol for awareness and communication that promotes respect for different cultures and helps prevent similar situations.”

Kylian Mbappe: What has the reaction been in China?

On Tuesday morning, four topics related to Mbappe remained among the top 10 trending searches on China’s social media platform, Weibo, Reuters reported.

The report said some internet critics had called ​for China to blacklist Mbappe and “reduce his commercial value to zero”, receiving hundreds of likes in response.

Reuters cited a spokesperson for China’s Foreign Ministry as saying that words and actions that hurt the feelings of the Chinese people “will naturally be met with joint opposition from all sectors of Chinese society.”

Confirmed Chinese brands to have dropped Mbappe

The country’s largest dairy producer, Mengniu, is immediately ceasing work with Mbappe, saying it “firmly opposes and has a zero-tolerance policy towards any words or actions that hurt the feelings of the Chinese people”.

The Shanghai Milkground ​Food Tech and Eastroc Beverage have followed suit, while drinks giant Dongpeng reportedly said the company “firmly opposes and has a zero-tolerance policy towards any behaviour that offends national sentiments.”

EFL Cup draw: Quarter-final lowdown including time, TV channel and stream

Draw details for the 2026/27 EFL Cup quarter-finals

Last Update:

The 2026/27 EFL Cup is about to go down to the final eight with the first quarter-finals in a major English competition of the season.

This season’s last-16 ties included a meeting between record 10-time champions Liverpool and Chelsea, who they beat in the 2023/24 final.

Manchester City will match the Reds’ record if they lift the trophy this season and Enzo Maresca’s side also faced an all-Premier League tie to reach the quarter-finals, facing Brighton & Hove Albion.

Here are all the details on how to watch the draw for the 2026/27 EFL Cup quarter-finals, including date, time, TV channel and live streams.

Carabao Cup: When is the draw for the EFL Cup quarter finals?

The draw will take place on Wednesday, October 28 after the tie between Andoni Iraola’s team and the Blues.

Presenter Dave Jones will host the draw alongside former England defenders Conor Coady and Graeme Le Saux.

What time is the EFL Cup quarter final draw?

The game at Anfield kicks off at 20:00 GMT (16:00 ET / 13:00 PT) and will go straight to penalties if the scoreline is level after 90 minutes.

That means the draw is likely to take place at approximately 22:00 GMT (18:00 ET / 15:00 PT), depending on added time and whether spot kicks are required.

All eight ties are on Sky Sports, with the game between Liverpool and Chelsea also available on ITV1.

Via Now TV, Sky Sports costs £14.99 for a day membership, £28 a month for a 12-month membership or £34.99 a month with no contract.

EFL Cup fifth round draw ball numbers

EFL Cup dates 2026/27: When are the Carabao Cup quarter-finals?

Do EFL Cup quarter final ties go to extra time, replays and penalties?

Should they finish level after 90 minutes, EFL Cup ties go straight to penalties until the semi-finals, which take place over two legs.

If the scoreline is level after the second leg, extra time and – if necessary – penalties are used to separate teams.

The final is a one-off match at Wembley Stadium, with extra time and penalties used if required.

The EFL Cup winners receive a place in the play-off stage of the UEFA Conference League unless they qualify through another route for European competition.

Newcastle were an example of the rule in action in 2024/25, instead qualifying for the Champions League through their league position.

That meant their Conference League play-off place went to the next-highest ranked team who had not qualified for European competition via their league position.

articles.summary: Fleetwood recorded one of the great EFL Cup shocks
articles.content:
Fleetwood goalkeeper Lynch: We took inspiration from Grimsby beating Manchester United last year

Fleetwood recorded one of the great EFL Cup shocks

Last Update:

Fleetwood Town goalkeeper Jay Lynch said his side took inspiration from Grimsby beating Manchester United last year as they became the second League Two within the space of a year to knock a giant out of the Carabao Cup.

The Cod Army triumphed 5-3 on penalties to knock out Premier League champions Arsenal in the last 16 after a 1-1 draw in normal time for a victory which will go down as one of the greatest in League Cup history.

It was via penalties that fellow League Two side Grimsby dumped out Man Utd in the second round last year, but Fleetwood’s achievements may just top that after knocking out last year’s Premier League winners and Champions League finalists.

Keeper Lynch played a huge part, making a number of huge saves including one to deny Bruno Guimaraes in the shootout, and was ready to take in the jubilant scenes at HIghbury.

He told Sky Sports: “My voice has gone from organising the defence.

“The whole team throughout the game was magnificent. To beat the English champions – credit to these lads.

“We took heart from Grimsby beating Man Utd last year. We kind of compared it.

“A typical night in Fleetwood. We were expecting a storm, we knew the conditions would be horrible, so we thought it might go in our favour.

“Amazing for the club, the town. Honestly it means everything to everyone.”

Fleetwood boss Lawlor: The club’s greatest night

Fleetwood Town boss Matt Lawlor revelled in Fleetwood’s epic night, which he declared the best in the club’s history, having been a non-league side for much of their existence prior to 2012.

He said to Sky Sports: “It’s really hard to address the players. I’ve just said to enjoy it and then we’ve got a league game on Saturday and I didn’t want to be the bearer of the reality, but we’ve got a game. I just can’t believe it.

“The biggest night in the club’s history in terms of opposition coming to town and we’ve managed to beat the champions.

“We knew before the game, we’re not stupid enough and not egotistical enough that you think we’re going to go to the best team in the country and the most organised team in the country and the best of the basics and the world-class players, in that we’re going to go and outplay them.

“So we had to ride our luck, we had to deny space, we had to deny options for them. And I think we did that really, really well in terms of the majority of the game.

“Obviously, the goal happens, but they’re going to happen; they’re so good at football. The footballers that they have, the gaps that they find and we see it every week in the Premier League.

“I’m a big football fan and I watch the National League all the way through to the Premier League, Championship.

“So for me it was a tough game to prepare for, but I’m just so glad that the lads have the feeling the way they are and took that performance into make that town, the club, everyone proud.”

articles.title: Messi deserved Ballon d’Or and Kane’s triumph won’t ‘remove the stain’ of England’s World Cup semi-final defeat – Ole
articles.summary: Lionel Messi came fifth in the Ballon d'Or voting but one Argentinian newspaper says he deserved to win
articles.content:
Messi deserved Ballon d’Or and Kane’s triumph won’t ‘remove the stain’ of England’s World Cup semi-final defeat – Ole

Lionel Messi came fifth in the Ballon d'Or voting but one Argentinian newspaper says he deserved to win

Last Update:

Argentinian newspaper Ole claims Lionel Messi should have won the Ballon d’Or and insisted Harry Kane’s triumph “won’t remove the stain” of England’s World Cup semi-final defeat.

In an editorial, the newspaper suggested 2026 was a year in which the eight-time winner “most deserved” the award due to his exploits at the summer showpiece with Messi leading his country to the final where they lost to Spain.

Argentina beat England in a bad-tempered last-four clash after two late goals gave Lionel Scaloni’s side a 2-1 victory.

Messi, who did not travel to London for the ceremony – opting instead to attend the Messi Cup, an international youth tournament that carries his name – finished fifth in the voting, behind Kane, Kylian Mbappe, Lamine Yamal and Rodri.

He had returned to the shortlist for the first time in three years, at the age of 39, after also starring for Inter Miami, helping them win a maiden MLS Cup in December.

Ole commented: “Kane didn’t win the World Cup but achieved personal recognition. Among the merits of the 33-year-old striker we must recognise the incredible figure of 73 goals and 81 goal involvements [in 2026] between Bayern Munich and England.

“His performance at the World Cup also allowed him to leave Gary Lineker behind as England’s top scorer in the history of the tournament. With 14 goals to his name, he consolidated an outstanding trajectory that already had a highlight in Russia 2018, an edition in which he claimed the Golden Boot with six goals.

“Although the stain of having been defeated by Messi and Argentina, in the semi-finals in 2026, is one that will never be removed.”

‘The best will always be Leo Messi’

The article concluded: “With as many reasons as the other stars to have been chosen winner of this Ballon d’Or, the scoring record of a player with an exemplary profile was enough to give him the edge in one of the most even editions of recent times.

“But for us, the best is and always will be Leo Messi. The World Cup, once again, gave us evidence why.”

Messi recently retired from international football but continues to be a force in Major League Soccer.

He has a league-leading 25 goals this season but was left on the bench for the weekend defeat at the New York Red Bulls after making a trans-Atlantic dash back from Spain where he received the prestigious Princess of Asturias Award for Sports.

Messi is expected to return to the starting line-up when Miami face Cincinnati on Wednesday night.

articles.title: Michael Carrick dodges Manchester United sack AGAIN and will be in charge for Chelsea clash
articles.summary: Manchester United will give Michael Carrick another opportunity to prove he can be a success at Old Trafford
articles.content:
Michael Carrick dodges Manchester United sack AGAIN and will be in charge for Chelsea clash

Manchester United will give Michael Carrick another opportunity to prove he can be a success at Old Trafford

Last Update:

Michael Carrick will get another chance to steady the ship at Manchester United with the club having no plans to sack him before Saturday’s game at Chelsea.

United chiefs have spent two days assessing Carrick’s role at Old Trafford following the 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth on Sunday but have opted against dismissing him and he will instead prepare the squad for the game at Stamford Bridge.

The news comes as something of a surprise given the game against Bournemouth was supposed to be Carrick’s final opportunity, coming just five days after a 4-1 humbling at Como in the Champions League.

United produced another lifeless performance against the Cherries, who could have won by a much larger margin than 3-0, a result that left Carrick’s side fifth bottom of the Premier League with just seven points from eight games.

The former England midfielder has presided over United’s worst top-flight start in 40 years and their worst of the Premier League era.

United will head to Chelsea on the back of an eight-game winless run in all competitions. They are not in EFL Cup action this week, having spurned a 2-0 lead to lose 3-2 at home to Brighton & Hove Albion in the third round.

Carrick has dilemma over United skipper Fernandes

Carrick was at the club’s Carrington training ground yesterday to watch United’s Under-21 side in a behind-closed-doors against Hull and took training as normal on Tuesday.

It was his first interaction with the first-team squad following Sunday’s game after which he appeared to say an emotional farewell to the United supporters, who sang his name before turning their ire on the players.

Carrick has a big decision to make regarding Bruno Fernandes’ involvement against Chelsea. The captain was left on the bench for the Bournemouth game after questioning the manager’s tactics in the defeat to Como.

He failed to make an appearance despite United’s struggles with Carrick instead bringing on the likes of Joshua Zirkzee and Shea Lacey.

It seems inconceivable the current PFA Player of the Year will start among the substitutes against Chelsea with Carrick’s job one again on the line.

If it does go wrong against Xabi Alonso’s men then United could be forced to make a change even though the contenders to succeed Carrick at Old Trafford look largely uninspiring.

The list is headed by Eddie Howe, who won one EFL Cup title at Newcastle despite a lavish spending spree under their Saudi Arabian owners, and also contains the likes of Antonio Conte and Julian Nagelsmann.

articles.title: Why Kylian Mbappe and La Liga have said sorry to China
articles.summary: Kylian Mbappe came second in the Men's Ballon d'Or on Monday
articles.content:
Why Kylian Mbappe and La Liga have said sorry to China

Kylian Mbappe came second in the Men's Ballon d'Or on Monday

Last Update:

Kylian Mbappe has apologised for hurting “many people in China and Chinese communities around the world”.

Real Madrid forward Mbappe said an “ill-judged” comment was “absolutely not my intention” following a reported backlash in the country over alleged remarks he made on YouTube show The Bridge, which is hosted by Blancos teammate Aurelien Tchouameni.

The top scorer in Spain last season issued a statement shortly after La Liga apologised to Chinese football fans on behalf of clubs, offered “respect” to China and said it is working on plans to build awareness of “different cultures”.

Chinese brands have dropped Mbappe over the reported remarks about “a Chinese dictator”, followed by a meme of his face being superimposed on an image resembling late Chinese leader Mao Zedong, according to the BBC.

Kylian Mbappe: Full apology to people in China

“During a recent interview, I reacted to an image featuring myself,” said Mbappe. “My comment was ill-judged and I now understand that it hurt many people in China and in Chinese communities around the world.

“I apologise to everyone my words have upset. That was absolutely not my intention. I have deep respect for the Chinese people and their history and I am sincerely sorry.”

What is Kylian Mbappe alleged to have said about China?

In unverified clips online, Mbappe does not name Mao but says he uses the meme “all the time” with friends, adding that it “makes me laugh the most… there’s a video of a guy, I think it’s a Chinese dictator…”

Chinese football forum Dongqiudi reportedly highlighted the interview, calling it “inappropriate” and liable to “hurt the feelings of Chinese people”.

Mao is an icon of the Communist Party in China, where the internet and digital content are subject to strict state control and the former leader is one of the most closely regulated topics.

Satire or jokes about the country’s founding leader from 1949 until his death in 1976 are ⁠considered disrespectful and a social taboo.

The original video is not on The Bridge’s YouTube channel and it is unclear when the episode first aired.

Mbappe spoke in September about memes depicting him as a dictator. “Part of it is funny because you get the sense that, for some people, it’s all in good fun,” he told L’Equipe.

“There’s also a less funny part because we know the damage these kinds of people have caused throughout history.

“To be compared to people who murder others, or who have made millions and millions of people unhappy… I don’t think I’ve ever done anything like that in my life.

“So there’s a mix of things. On the one hand, I know it’s done in a light-hearted way and doesn’t go that far, but it sometimes shows a lack of political and human awareness in people.”

Kylian Mbappe: Full La Liga statement

La Liga said it “deeply regrets the offence caused” to Chinese fans. “These comments were made in a personal capacity and do not represent La Liga,” it added.

“To the extent of our institutional responsibility, we apologize on behalf of La Liga and all its clubs.

“Spanish football upholds respect, coexistence, and unity among people of all cultures. We convey our respect to China, its institutions and its people and we deeply value the support of the millions of fans who follow us each week.

“We reaffirm our commitment to a relationship built over years. We are working with our partners and institutional interlocutors in China to address this situation.

“Likewise, in collaboration with the clubs and players, we will implement a protocol for awareness and communication that promotes respect for different cultures and helps prevent similar situations.”

Kylian Mbappe: What has the reaction been in China?

On Tuesday morning, four topics related to Mbappe remained among the top 10 trending searches on China’s social media platform, Weibo, Reuters reported.

The report said some internet critics had called ​for China to blacklist Mbappe ⁠and “reduce his commercial value to zero”, receiving hundreds of likes in response.

Reuters cited a spokesperson for China’s Foreign Ministry as saying that words and actions that hurt the feelings of the Chinese people “will naturally be met with joint opposition from all sectors of Chinese society.”

Confirmed Chinese brands to have dropped Mbappe

The country’s largest dairy producer, Mengniu, is immediately ceasing work with Mbappe, saying it “firmly opposes and has a zero-tolerance policy towards any words or actions that hurt the feelings of the Chinese people”.

The Shanghai Milkground ​Food Tech and Eastroc Beverage have followed suit, while drinks giant Dongpeng reportedly said the company “firmly opposes and has a zero-tolerance policy towards any behaviour that offends national sentiments.”

The BBC cited a report by state-owned newspaper The Global Times that state broadcaster CCTV’s news apps will not feature Mbappe-related content and will stop showing La Liga matches.

articles.title: Carragher would have Real Madrid outcast Alexander-Arnold back at Liverpool…and give him plenty of stick!
articles.summary: Trent Alexander-Arnold left Liverpool under a cloud but the Reds' former centre-half Jamie Carragher would welcome him back to Anfield
articles.content:
Carragher would have Real Madrid outcast Alexander-Arnold back at Liverpool…and give him plenty of stick!

Trent Alexander-Arnold left Liverpool under a cloud but the Reds' former centre-half Jamie Carragher would welcome him back to Anfield

Last Update:

Jamie Carragher would love to see Trent Alexander-Arnold back at Liverpool.

Alexander-Arnold left Anfield for Real Madrid in controversial circumstances at the end of the 2024/25 season, the Spanish giants paying a reduced fee of around £10million after the full-back had run down his contract.

That undoubtedly tarnished the 28-year-old’s legacy on Merseyside, despite helping Liverpool to two Premier League titles, one Champions League crown, two EFL Cups and one FA Cup after coming through the club’s academy.

“I’d have him back,” said Carragher on the Overlap Fan Debate, brought to you by Sky Bet. “Give him plenty of stick… I think he made a mistake, I do. I think he made a big mistake. But, as I said, if something benefits Liverpool Football Club going forward… and we do have problems in terms of the right-back [position].

“Ronnie [Ronald Araujo] has been fantastic but we do have a problem in terms of full-backs passing. We’ve definitely missed his creativity.”

Trent is third-choice at Real Madrid – Carragher

Alexander-Arnold has failed to establish himself at Madrid, struggling for form and fitness under all three managers he has played for.

He started on the bench for Madrid’s Clasico win at Barcelona on Sunday, only appearing for the final few seconds as Jose Mourinho attempted to play down the clock.

Midfielder Federico Valverde started at right-back at Camp Nou and was replaced just after the hour mark by Denzel Dumfries.

Carragher added: “At the moment, he’s third choice right-back for Real Madrid. They’re playing a midfield player at right-back, and even in El Clásico, Denzel Dumfries, the first-choice right-back, if you like, comes on as a sub. So when you’re third choice at a club, they’re obviously wanting you to move on.”

Carragher believes Jacquet is first-choice at Liverpool

Should Alexander-Arnold return to Liverpool he would likely line up alongside Jeremy Jacquet, who has impressed next to Virgil van Dijk following his move from Rennes.

“I think he’s the first-choice centre-back and starting to look after Virgil a little bit rather than the other way around,” Carragher said of the France international. “And even though he’s only played eight games, I already feel he’s an upgrade on everybody else Virgil’s played alongside. I know it’s early to say that, but he really does look the part.

“And Virgil was always going to need that at some stage where he just has to play his own game. He can’t look after a back four. He can’t look after a centre-back partner. I think we’re at that stage now with Van Dijk, still playing well, but he should just be left to play his own game.”

‘Liverpool could be in a title race if they beat Arsenal’

Liverpool have lost just once in all competitions this season – 3-0 hammering at home to Manchester City – and sit fourth in the Premier League table following the weekend victory over Brighton.

They face Chelsea in the EFL Cup on Wednesday night before a big Premier League clash with champions Arsenal on Sunday.

Carragher said: “The thing I like right now is the fact that they’re getting results, things are going well, but I still think there’s a lot of improvement [to come]. When I watch the games, I still don’t think Liverpool have had one 90 minutes where you go, ‘everything was proper’. You know, three or four nil win, got the goals, looked solid at the back, kept the ball.

“I’ve never believed Liverpool are in a title race this season. But if you beat the champions and you’re closer in the table…

“We all look at [Andoni] Iraola’s squad and we probably say he’s been dealt a bad hand to a certain extent. What could Liverpool do in January that could propel them into a title race? If obviously the situation with [Manchester] City is resolved and they’re not actually in the title race, and you’re thinking it’s just Arsenal? It’s not actually the two teams we think we need to overtake, there’s just one now.”

articles.title: Bayern coach gives Vincent Kompany update: ‘He’s very calm’
articles.summary: Vincent Kompany has won the Bundesliga in each of his Bayern seasons
articles.content:
Bayern coach gives Vincent Kompany update: ‘He’s very calm’

Vincent Kompany has won the Bundesliga in each of his Bayern seasons

Last Update:

Bayern Munich assistant head coach Aaron Danks says manager Vincent Kompany is yet to receive a diagnosis after collapsing at the club’s training ground on Friday but is “in good spirits” in hospital and appears to be “getting better”.

Former Belgium and Manchester City defender Kompany missed Bayern’s 3-1 win at Freiburg in the Bundesliga on Sunday and received a “short visit” from Danks on Monday, the former Aston Villa coaching staff member said.

“He’s very calm,” said Danks, calling the improvement he perceived in Kompany’s condition “really positive”.

“It’s [about] letting him recover, rest and take his time, so nothing changes there. We had some good conversations but we kept it away from the football specifics, the tactics specifics.

“He asked how everything went, he asked how the players were. Apart from that, it was just a friendly chat. It was nice to see him and catch up.”

What happened to Vincent Kompany?

The 40-year-old had been suffering from a virus and missed Bayern’s press conference a day before their home game against Arsenal in the Champions League last Wednesday.

Kompany took charge for the 2-2 draw but collapsed while watching Bayern’s reserve team two days later.

“The fact is, we protect our coach wherever we can,” Roten director of sport Max Eberl said after Kompany was admitted.

“If a coach says he feels ready to do something, then we’re not going to say ‘we won’t allow that’ if we don’t know what’s going on.

“It’s also everyone’s own responsibility to say ‘I can’t carry on now’.”

How long has Vincent Kompany been in hospital for?

Kompany had been in hospital for four days when Danks spoke on October 27, a day before Bayern were scheduled to host second-tier Magdeburg in the second round of the German Cup.

When could Vincent Kompany return after collapse?

“There are no major updates in terms of diagnosis or return to work – nothing like that at the moment,” said Danks.

Eberl emphasised that everyone at the club should be “clear” on expecting Kompany to return in weeks rather than days.

“Vinnie will be given all the time he needs,” added Eberl. “We’re not starting to put together any timeframes.

“We need to firstly figure out what it is. Then we’ll discuss calmly what the recovery time is to be.”

Ballon d’Or 2026: Harry Kane triumph makes Aaron Danks ‘proud’

Danks admitted that he had not necessarily expected Bayern talisman Harry Kane to win the Ballon d’Or on Monday.

“I can’t say I was overly confident – he had to hold his own against top players,” explained Danks. “The margins were very tight.

“We work very closely with him and see the effort he puts in. As an Englishman, I’m not entirely impartial here, but I see how hard he works every day.

“I’m delighted for him and also for the club; it shows what the club stands for. I’m very proud. I’m also very pleased that Harry has won this for England, as the first player to do so since Michael Owen [in 2001].

“He’ll now come back and carry on in his usual professional and humble way.”

Some observers have speculated that Kane’s remarks about being willing to “work hard in silence” and “let success be your noise” may have been directed at the likes of rival Lamine Yamal.

“Harry’s statement was fantastic for all young players; he wasn’t addressing it to anyone in particular,” said Danks.

“He works incredibly hard to be well prepared. His success speaks for itself. A few years ago, many people said he’d never win anything.

“Those things are coming his way now; he’s letting his success speak for itself.”

Bayern Munich fixtures, schedule

Kane could feature when holders Bayern play their German Cup tie. “It’s a fantastic moment for him and a great achievement,” said Danks.

“He’ll be reporting back with the other players that travelled. They’re due back at lunchtime [on Tuesday], so he’ll practice this afternoon and be available.”

Bayern then face Borussia Dortmund in the Bundesliga in Der Klassiker on Saturday.

articles.title: Guti reveals conspiracy theory as Kane’s Ballon d’Or success falls flat in Spain
articles.summary: Harry Kane's Ballon d'Or win has not gone down well in Spain and the conspiracy theories have already started
articles.content:
Guti reveals conspiracy theory as Kane’s Ballon d’Or success falls flat in Spain

Harry Kane's Ballon d'Or win has not gone down well in Spain and the conspiracy theories have already started

Last Update:

Former Real Madrid midfielder Guti has poured scorn on the decision to award Harry Kane with the Ballon d’Or and claimed even the Bayern Munich striker didn’t think he’d win.

Kane was last night crowned the best player in the world in recognition of a brilliant season for Bayern and England in which he scored 73 goals, helping his club side retain the Bundesliga and England reach the semi-finals of the World Cup.

The 33-year-old became the first Englishman to win the award in 25 years but Guti felt closest challengers Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe both had stronger cases.

He told El Chiringuito: “It’s quite a coincidence that they take the 70th anniversary Ballon d’Or ceremony to London and someone from London wins it. What a coincidence, right? An incredible coincidence. Lamine and Mbappé deserved it more.

“Just look at Kane’s face when they announced his name. He never imagined in his life that he would win the Ballon d’Or. He thought Lamine and Mbappé would finish ahead of him. You don’t react like that when you win the Ballon d’Or if you think you deserve it. He didn’t even know how to put his jacket on.”

Kane doesn’t excite me, says former Arsenal man Nasri

Although the majority of the reaction has been overwhelmingly positive to Kane’s triumph with the former Tottenham man declining in the build-up to indulge in the self-promotion that always accompanies challengers from Spain, former Arsenal rival Samir Nasri was another who felt there were more suitable recipients.

Nadri said: “Harry Kane, Ballon d’Or winner… OK, the statistics made the difference, and he’s a great player. But he never led his team to a major trophy, nor was he decisive in the games that really mattered. He doesn’t excite me. I couldn’t care less.”

El Larguero even wheeled out one of Yamal’s uncles to express his disappointment at his nephew’s third-placed finish.

Abdul said: “Very sad, my nephew is the best player in the world, everyone knows it. If you like soccer, you’re going to watch Lamine, not Harry Kane. Kane is a great goalscorer, but Lamine shines on the field. Lamine is young, he has time and that’s why they don’t give it to him. Kane only has three years of football left, that’s why he was given it. I’m sure Lamine will end up winning five [Ballons d’Or]. In three days Lamine’s sadness will pass.”

There was one dignified message from Spain with Real Madrid TV stating: “Kane is the Ballon d’Or. Congratulations to the player of Bayern and the English national team. The forecasts have been right and we must wait for another opportunity for Mbappé. This Ballon d’Or for Kane is far from undeserved. He’s a great player and has had a great career.”

Kane is an asset for Bayern – Eberl

Unsurprisingly the reaction was different in Germany and from Bayern in particular.

The club’s sporting director Max Eberl said: “Harry Kane is an asset for FC Bayern and would be for any team in the world. He takes responsibility, on the field and in the dressing room; he is someone everyone else follows, day after day. This title is the reward for his impressive achievements in his career as a whole.

“Harry deserves all the honours in the world, and the fact that he has been awarded the Ballon d’Or here in his home town sends a wonderful message to everyone, that you should never give up. We are delighted with all the nominations – FC Bayern is a stage for world-class talent.”

Kane will parade the trophy in front of the Bayern fans ahead of the DFB-Pokal clash with Magdeburg at the Allianz Arena on Wednesday night.

articles.title: Ballon d’Or Men’s Player of the Year winner: Harry Kane becomes first English winner for 25 years
articles.summary: Get the latest on the winner of the Men's Ballon d'Or Player of the Year awards
articles.content:
Ballon d’Or Men’s Player of the Year winner: Harry Kane becomes first English winner for 25 years

Get the latest on the winner of the Men's Ballon d'Or Player of the Year awards

Last Update:

Harry Kane has become the first Englishman to win the Ballon d’Or for 25 years after being crowned the winner at Monday’s ceremony in London.

Kane scored a sensational 73 goals for Bayern Munich and England in 2025-26, while he won the Bundesliga title for the second time.

The last English winner last came in 2001 when Michael Owen won the award, while he is only the fifth English player to win it ever after inaugural victor Stanley Matthews (1956), Bobby Charlton (1966) and Kevin Keegan (1978 and 1979) the others.

Kane said: “I am almost speechless. Being here in London has made it extra special. Made it a good omen for me tonight. Thank you to everyone who voted for me. I can imagine it was tough this year.

“Some world-class players in the room tonight. Congratulations to all the winners and nominees tonight and impressive showing determination and hard work can really achieve.”

Kane dedicates award to Kompany

Kane scored 61 goals in 51 club matches last season as the striker won the league title and cup in Germany last season.

He was quick to wish his best to club manager Vincent Kompany, who was unable to attend the awards after collapsing at Bayern Munich’s training ground.

Kane said: “Without you guys [Bayern Munich team-mates] and the rest of the team it wouldn’t be possible, the way you guys push me, the way we compete. So thank you very much.

“To Vinny [Vincent Kompany]. I know he is at home or still in the hospital. Wishing you well. I hope this gave you a bit of energy. To all the staff we way train and the way you push us it is a credit to yourself.

“Since I have been with you I have improved as player, improved as a person and a leader. Thanks to your leadership. An honour to play for Bayern Munich.

“To represent you is a real privilege. Glad to be bringing this trophy back to Bayern Munich.”

Kane salutes England team-mates

Kane also scored 12 goals for England during the 2025-26 season, including six at the World Cup, albeit they fell short and lost in the semi-finals.

“To my England team-mates, again the same,” Kane added. “We had a special year. It wasn’t the perfect year, but we had a load of great moments. We built a great bond together.

“The togetherness in the hotel in the World Cup. An honour to captain you and lead you. It makes me extremely proud. This one is for all of us for sure.

“Thomas Tuchel and the staff at England, again the leadership the way you drive us, the way you push standards is something to be admired.”

Kane’s record-breaking season in numbers

Harry Kane delivered a remarkable 61 goals for Bayern Munich across all competitions, finishing 19 ahead of any other player in Europe’s top five leagues.

His tally included 36 Bundesliga goals, 14 in the Champions League and 10 in the German Cup, where he scored a hat-trick in the 3-0 final victory over Stuttgart.

His dominance extended beyond club football, with 12 goals for England, including six at the World Cup, taking his combined season total to 73 goals.

He also helped Bayern secure the German domestic double, adding to the Bundesliga title he had won the previous season.

That total of 73 placed Kane among the most prolific goalscorers in football history. Only Lionel Messi has recorded more goals in a single season for club and country among players from Europe’s top leagues, scoring 82 in 2011–12.

Kane’s campaign surpassed the tallies of several legendary forwards, including Gerd Müller, Cristiano Ronaldo, Erling Haaland and Luis Suarez.

Ballon d’Or Men’s Player of the Year leaderboard

1) Harry Kane – Bayern Munich and England2) Kylian Mbappé – Real Madrid and France3) Lamine Yamal – Barcelona and Spain4) Rodri – Barcelona and Spain5) Lionel Messi – Inter Miami and Argentina6) Khvicha Kvaratskhelia – PSG and Georgia7) Ousmane Dembélé – PSG and France8) Erling Haaland – Manchester City and Norway9) Michael Olise – Bayern Munich and France10) Fabián Ruiz – PSG and Spain11) Jude Bellingham – Real Madrid and England12) Pau Cubarsi – Barcelona and Spain13) Achraf Hakimi – PSG and Morocco14) Vitinha – PSG and Portugal15) Declan Rice – Arsenal and England16) Ferran Torres – Barcelona/PSG and Spain17) Vinicius Junior – Real Madrid and Brazil18) Marc Cucurella – Chelsea/Real Madrid and Spain19) Joao Neves – PSG and Portugal20) Willian Pacho – PSG and Ecuador21) Gabriel – Arsenal and Brazil22) Lautaro Martinez – Inter Milan and Argentina23) Nuno Mendes – PSG and Portugal24) Luis Diaz – Bayern Munich and Colombia25) Marquinhos – PSG and Brazil26) Dayot Upamecano – Bayern Munich and France27) Bruno Fernandes – Man Utd and Portugal28) Julian Quinones – Al Qadsiah and Mexico29=) William Saliba – Arsenal and France29=) Sadio Mane – Al Nassr and Senegal

articles.summary: The latest updates from the Ballon d'Or 2026
articles.content:
Who won the Ballon d’Or 2026? Recap on the results live from London as they happened

The latest updates from the Ballon d'Or 2026

Last Update:

The most prestigious individual prizes in football were handed out in London as the 70th Ballon d’Or ceremony takes place on Monday.

The award has been co-organised with UEFA since 2024, with Aitana Bonmati and Ousmane Dembele lifting the headline women’s and men’s honours in 2025.

Spain and London City Lionesses schemer Alexia Putellas and Bayern Munich and England talisman Harry Kane were the winners in the women’s and men’s award, with a host of other winners across the night. Read on to see how the night unfolded.

22:55 GMT: Harry Kane wins Ballon d’Or!

He’s done it! Harry Kane has finally landed the Ballon d’Or in his hometown of London.

He’s the first Englishman to do so since Michael Owen in 2005. What a moment!

Check out the full story on the historic moment here.

22:35 GMT: Putellas wins Women’s Player of the Year

The overwhelming favourite has won the award as Alexia Putellas wins Women’s Player of the Year for the third time in her career.

Putellas now turns out for WSL side London City Lionesses but won the Women’s Champions League with Barcelona last season.

Check out the full story here.

22:15 GMT: Kane wins Best Goalscorer award

He’ll hope to be celebrating again in a few minutes’ time, but Harry Kane has ended the night with an award after winning the Men’s Best Goalscorer award.

The Bayern Munich striker scored a sensational 73 goals for club and country in 2025-26.

The Women’s Striker of the Year goes to Charlyn Corral. The first ever Mexican to win a Ballon d’Or and also has impressive record with 47 goals in 47 games.

22:02 GMT: Paris Saint-Germain win Men’s Club of the Year

Champions League winners for the second year running, Paris Saint-Germain have capped off a wonderful 2026 with another award for their collection, which they also claimed last year.

The Parisians also lifted the Ligue 1 title, with last year’s Ballon d’Or winner Ousmane Dembele here to collect the award.

Dembele said: “On behalf of all the Paris St-Germain club, I would like to say thank you to the president and sporting director, all the staff and, of course, our coach, Luis Enrique.

“Our fans always support us, and always stand behind us. We have created an incredible club, and we always fight together side by side.”

21:50 GMT: Another award for Barcelona!

Yet another award for Barcelona as their clean sweep of the women’s awards continue as they win the Women’s Club of the Year.

They won the Women’s Champions League for the fourth time and Liga F for the 11th time and are deserving winners, with their coach, goalkeeper and best youngster all claiming individuakl awards on the night.

21:45 GMT: Saka wins Socrates Award

Bukayo Saka has been named the winner of the Socrates Award for his workl with charity BigShoe, which helps disadvantaged children have opportunities in football.

Saka said: “I would like to thank France football for the opportunity to be here. Keep raising awareness of these causes that are close to my heart.

“For me, it is an honour to be here and an honour to receive this award. On behalf of all the children, we have been able to help. Thank you.”

20:35 GMT: Simon and Coll win goalkeeper awards

The Ballon d’Or Goalkeeper of the Year awards have been announced for Men and Women and it is another two awards for Spain as Cata Coll and Unai Simon are announced as winners.

Coll won the Women’s Champions League with Barcelona, while Simon was equally impressive as Spain won the men’s World Cup.

20:22 GMT: De la Fuente wins coach award

Luis de la Fuente is the winner of the Men’s Coach of the Year award! The 65-year-old guided his country to a World Cup triumph for only the second time.

He said: “Good evening, it is a real honour for me to receive this prize.

“To be among these nominees is just something very special. I would like to thank the rest of the nominees as they have done more than enough to deserve this.

“This prize is not an individual prize. This is for a whole team, a great team.

“It is an honour to train you and work with you. I would like to thank the Spanish football federation.

“The secret is really working with footballers that are very generous and work in solidarity and put their team above their individual selves.”

21:15 GMT: Men’s award up next

After a scheduled commercial break, we will find out who the Men’s Coach of the Year winner is. The nominees feature two current Premier League managers among a five-manager shortlist:

21:10 GMT: Pere Romeu named women’s coach winner

It’s been a great night for Barcelona so far as they continue their clean sweep of the awards so far as Barcelona women manager wins the Women’s Coach of the Year.

Romeu guided Barcelona to a triumph in the Women’s Champions League and won Liga F for the second successive time.

21:00 GMT: Lopez wins women’s youngster award

It is also back-to-back awards for a Barcelona player in the women’s Young Talent award as Vicky Lopez scoops up the award once again!

20:50 GMT: Yamal scoops young player of the year award

The first award, the Young Talent of the Year, has gone to one of the favourites in the Men’s Player of the Year award Lamine Yamal, who has scooped up the award for the third time.

Could this mean the main award is going to either Kane or Mbappe?

20:45 GMT: We are finally underway!

Some 45 minutes later than planned, seemingly due to the central London traffic, the Ballon d’Or 2026 ceremony is underway, with British singer Jorja Smith kicking things off with a performance.

Stay tuned for all the latest updates as they happen. A reminder of all the winners that will be announced tonight:

Ballon d’Or Women’s Player of the Year winner: Putellas wins award for third time

Get the latest on the Ballon d'Or Women's Player of the Year winner

Last Update:

Alexia Putellas has been named the Women’s Player of the Year at the 2026 Ballon d’Or awards.

The Spain international has scooped the award for the third time after captaining Barcelona to a continental quadruple in 2025-26, winning the Liga F, Cope de la Reina, Spanish Super Cup and Champions League.

She became Barcelona’s joint-second top scorer of all time after scoring two goals in the Champions League semi-final in May, and earned the player of the tournament award in the process.

She equals her former team-mate Bonmati’s record of three awards, having also been a key part of Spain’s Nations League-winning side.

Putellas said: “Thank you very much. It is a pleasure to be here, again.

“Thank you to the ones who thought I deserved this award. I don’t know what to say, too many things! Congrats to all the nominees, congrats to all the winners.

“I want to start by saying thank you team-mates.

“I think anyone here could have fairly won this trophy and be giving this speech here right now.

“A great pleasure to play alongside each and every single one of you.

“Incredible experiences as a team, we overcome some difficulties, some injuries, some moments we weren’t expecting as a team and a great pride for me as captain.”

Putellas is the fifth representative of Barcelona to win an award during Monday’s ceremony in London, with Vicky Lopez and Lamine Yamal winning the Young Player of the Year awards in the men’s and women’s cateogires.

Barca Femini coach Pere Romeu won the Women’s Coach of the Year, with goalkeeper Cata Coll claiming Women’s Goalkeeper of the Year and Barcelona winning Women’s Club of the Year.

The winners of the 2026 Ballon d’Or Goalkeeper of the Year winners have been announced with Unai Simon and Cata Coll scooping up the awards.

Simon has picked up the award for the first time after conceding only one goal as Spain won the World Cup in the summer.

The Athletic Bilbao stopper said: “Well done Cata [Coll]. A real honour for me to be here this evening.

articles.content:
Chaos at the Ballon d’Or! Statement released after Kane, Mbappe, Yamal and Messi all announced as winners

Last Update:

The Ballon d’Or were forced to release a statement after accidentally publishing several articles on their official site all announcing different winners ahead of Monday’s ceremony.

Harry Kane, Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe all had articles published on them winning the coveted award, with the three articles later deleted.

A subsequent statement from a Ballon d’Or spokesperson said: “Portraits of some Ballon d’Or nominees prepared by Ballondor.com were inadvertently published online.

“These articles had been prepared in advance for all nominees in the event of a win. They DO NOT, in any way, reveal the podium, which remains unknown to everyone at this time.”

The Ballon d’Or ceremony, hosted in London, has now been pushed back to 8:30pm GMT, which is unknown to be a result of the article mistakes.

Ballon d’Or”: Kane prematurely named winner

An article naming Harry Kane as the winner of the 2026 Ballon d’Or began circulating online shortly after 17:15 GMT on Monday, more than four hours before the ceremony was due to begin at London’s Palladium Theatre.

The piece, published on the award’s official website, sparked confusion over whether organisers France Football had accidentally revealed the winner after journalists voted at the end of September.

However, further investigation revealed similar articles had also been published for other leading contenders, including Barcelona’s Yamal and Real Madrid’s Mbappe.

What time is the Ballon d’Or ceremony 2026? Full start details, confirmed timings

All the details on Ballon d'Or 2026 timings

Last Update:

Created by France Football in 1956, the most prestigious individual prizes in football will be awarded in London when the 70th Ballon d’Or ceremony takes place on Monday.

The award has been co-organised with UEFA since 2024, with Aitana Bonmati and Ousmane Dembele lifting the headline women’s and men’s honours in 2025.

Spain and London City Lionesses schemer Alexia Putellas is being tipped to end Barcelona and Roja magician Bonmati’s three-year run in the Ballon d’Or Feminin this time.

Bayern Munich and England talisman Harry Kane is the favourite in the men’s category after an extraordinarily prolific year, ahead of Real Madrid’s Kylian Mbappe, who won the Golden Boot at the World Cup 2026 with France and top-scored in La Liga last season.

What time is the Ballon d’Or 2026?

Here are the key scheduled timings for the ceremony.

When does the Ballon d’Or 2026 ceremony start?

Here are the scheduled start times for the ceremony. You can also visit the Ballon d’Or worldwide timings list.

Why is the Ballon d’Or 2026 in London?

Paris’ Theatre du Chatelet has hosted the Ballon d’Or since 2019 but the ceremony will move to the London Palladium this year.

The first Ballon d’Or ceremony in London is a tribute to Sir Stanley Matthews, the English inaugural recipient of the golden ball.

L’Equipe editor Gabriel Hanot gave Matthews the award on December 18 1956 in a wood-panelled room at Blackpool Town Hall. Matthews is said to have responded with a “truncated speech” and received a “smattering of applause”.

“He was a pioneer,” the Ballon d’Or’s official account says of Matthews.

“Continually pushing the boundaries in diet and fitness and adopting methodologies that, at the time, were considered quirky at best by scoffing team-mates, but which are now cornerstones of modern-day practices.

“He was years ahead of the curve. Decades. And though it was only a ceremony of sorts, and though this year’s gala is being held 250 miles south of the Lancashire coastline, it can be stated that this autumn football is coming home. Back to where the Ballon d’Or all began.”

Ballon d’Or 2026 ceremony: Who’s hosting and performing?

Hugely popular journalist Kate Scott will be on expert hosting duties alongside familiar CBS Sports sidekick Thierry Henry.

France legend Henry was nominated for the Ballon d’Or nine times, finishing second in 2003.

Musicians Jorja Smith and French Montana will perform and organisers are promising “further surprises”.

British singer-songwriter Smith blends R&B, soul, jazz and electronic influences and will open the ceremony by performing her 2016 single, Blue Lights, to mark 10 years since the release of the record.

Morocco-born, Bronx raised Montana is a three-time Grammy-nominated hiphop star whose hits include the Diamond-certified Unforgettable, which featured Swae Lee, the five-time Platinum No Stylist with Drake and the six-time Platinum Lockjaw with Kodak Black.

Last Update:

Harry Kane is expected to become just the fifth Englishman to win the Ballon d’Or when the ceremony takes place in London tonight.

The Bayern Munich striker is the bookmakers’ favourite to be crowned the world’s best player at a glittering event – hosted by Thierry Henry and Kate Scott – at the Palladium Theatre.

Kane has had another wonderful year for Bayern and England, scoring 61 times for the Bundesliga giants in all competitions last season as they clinched another league and cup double. The 33-year-old also scored six times as England finished third at the World Cup.

Kylian Mbappe is thought to be Kane’s closest challenger. Mbappe scored 42 goals in 44 games for Real Madrid last season, and added another 10 in the United States, Canada and Mexico over the summer. But Madrid’s failure to land any major silverware could hamper his chances.

He will also arrive in London with a spring in his step after netting twice in Madrid’s Clasico win at Barcelona last night.

The same can’t be said for Lamine Yamal, who was on the losing side at Camp Nou. The teenager is regarded as third favourite to lift the trophy despite scoring 16 times as Barca retained the Liga trophy and playing a key role as Spain backed up their 2024 European Championship success by winning the World Cup.

Lionel Messi is believed to be an outsider.

Messi returned to the shortlist for the first time in three years following his remarkable performances at the World Cup, where he guided Argentina to the final before losing to Spain.

The 39-year-old also had another brilliant year with Inter Miami in the United States, helping them win a maiden MLS Cup in December.

Messi has won the award eight times previously but it would be a major surprise if he were to add a ninth.

If Kane does triumph he will join Kevin Keegan, Sir Bobby Charlton, Sir Stanley Matthews and Michael Owen in a small group of English winners.

articles.title: Cristiano Ronaldo needs Saudi Pro League to decide on 982nd career goal
articles.summary: Officials are assessing a potential Cristiano Ronaldo goal
articles.content:
Cristiano Ronaldo needs Saudi Pro League to decide on 982nd career goal

Officials are assessing a potential Cristiano Ronaldo goal

Last Update:

Cristiano Ronaldo may have to wait for his 982nd career goal if a Saudi Pro League meeting on Monday decides that the Al-Nassr captain’s header in his side’s 3-1 top-flight win at Al-Faisaly on Friday was an own-goal.

Five-time Ballon d’Or winner Ronaldo ran to celebrate after competing with opposition defender Andrei Girotto to apply the touch that diverted Joao Felix’s cross off a post and in for Al-Nassr’s second goal of the game, although replays appear to make the 41-year-old’s claim to have scored unclear.

Tariq Kayyal, the head of the league’s Compliance Committee, says officials are waiting on referee Abdullah Al-Owaidan’s statement and plan to “study all the reports”.

Will Cristiano Ronaldo be awarded Al Nassr goal?

While the Saudi Pro League highlights of the game suggest Ronaldo has been credited with the goal – the video is titled “Ronaldo gets GOAL 982” – official data providers appear to have attributed Girotto with the final touch.

“If we are convinced by them, we will decide whether to uphold or reject the decision, thus awarding the goal with the correct ruling,” Kayyal said of the perspectives his committee will consider, via Al-Riyadh.

Pundit and former Saudi Arabia midfielder Khalid Al-Shenaif reportedly said a refereeing committee had given the goal to Ronaldo.

Al-Shenaif is said to have claimed that the league has contacted data providers including experts Opta, “international platforms” and “possibly FIFA” to emphasise that the Madrid all-time top scorer headed the ball.

“That settles the matter,” The Nassr Tribune quoted Al-Shenaif as saying. “His tally stands at 982 goals.

“I believe the Saudi Pro League – or perhaps the Saudi Football Federation – will contact Opta… whose statistics are published across platforms worldwide, to confirm that the goal belongs to Ronaldo in accordance with the [refereeing committee verdict].”

On Monday morning, Opta’s match centre for the game credited Girotto with an own-goal.

How many goals has Cristiano Ronaldo scored?

Ronaldo scored his 981st career goal in a 3-1 home win over Uzbekistan Super League team Neftchi Fergana in the AFC Champions League on October 12.

As well as the enduring debate about whether Ronaldo or generational rival Lionel Messi is the best player of modern times, the Portugal icon’s status as the highest scorer ever has been questioned by some who consider Pele the leading marksman in history.

“All the goals [of mine] have videos,” Ronaldo told former Manchester United teammate Rio Ferdinand in 2024. “I will prove to the people, if they prefer this player… I don’t care about that.”

When will Cristiano Ronaldo score his 1,000th goal?

Speaking before the start of Portugal’s Nations League campaign in September, Ronaldo was asked whether he would prefer his 1,000th goal to be for Al-Nassr or Portugal.

“You know the answer: for the national team,” he replied. “It would be the culmination of a beautiful story. As the coach said: the cherry on top of the cake.”

The first camp under Portugal’s new head coach, Jorge Jesus, who led Al-Nassr to the Saudi title last season, ended in premature and acrimonious fashion for Ronaldo.

Having started Portugal’s first game at home to Wales, Ronaldo left the camp after remaining an unused substitute away to Norway on September 27 and discovering he would not start in Denmark on October 1.

In an elaborate statement, Ronaldo then said Jorge Jesus twice “broke his word” and committed an “absolute breach of trust”.

The Portuguese Football Federation has since given Ronaldo a 30-day suspension and fine of around £215 for the walk-out.

With Al-Nassr less than a third of the way through their season, Portugal in action less regularly and Ronaldo’s international future in doubt, his 1,000th goal is likeliest to arrive in this season’s Saudi Pro League.

Cristiano Ronaldo net worth

On financial website Forbes’ all-time list of the highest earning athletes in a year, only boxer Floyd Mayweather eclipses Ronaldo, having pocketed an estimated $300 million (£226m) in 2015 and $285m (£214.5m) in 2018.

Ronaldo was said to have surpassed $1 billion (£771m) in career earnings two years before becoming the most high-profile footballer to move to Saudi Arabia, making his Al-Nassr debut in January 2023.

Ronaldo’s first Al-Nassr deal was widely reported to be worth £14.75m a month or £3.4m per week. His annual salary was said to be £177m per year, made up of £62m for his football salary, supplemented by commercial bonuses.

Ronaldo has a variety of lucrative sponsorship deals, with his recent endorsements including Whoop, video game UFL and cryptocurrency exchange Binance.

Ronaldo won the Saudi title for the first time last season but failed to top-score in the top flight for the first time in his three seasons of being involved.

Shortly after Al-Nassr finished third in 2025/26 – 13 points behind Al-Ittihad – Ronaldo appeared to strongly hint on social media that he had played his final game for the club.

He agreed a new contract exactly a month later, having scored in Portugal’s triumphant Nations League semi-final against Germany and final against Spain.

He missed three matches in all competitions earlier this year, with Real Madrid’s all-time top scorer thought to have been unhappy at Al-Nassr’s perceived lack of transfer activity.

When is Ronaldo playing next? Al Nassr vs Al Wasl off

The AFC announced on Sunday that Al-Nassr’s Champions League home game against UAE Pro League side Al-Wasl on Monday would be postponed.

No reason was given for the decision, although Reuters cited the intensification of fighting in Yemen between a Saudi-led coalition and Iran-aligned ​Houthi forces, who have recently targeted Saudi airports including Riyadh.

Saudi teams have travelled by road for matches in the competition. The outlet said it had contacted Al-Wasl and the ⁠AFC ​for comment.

The Saudi Arabian Football Federation released a statement on Sunday saying arrangements for the game had been completed, including flight permits for Al-Wasl and the club’s national FA and the arrival of the match commissioner and refereeing team in Riyadh.

The federation “affirmed full support” for Al-Nassr and Saudi clubs in international competitions, voicing its “readiness to provide all necessary support and assistance in any legal actions taken by the clubs to protect their rights”.

articles.title: Jose Mourinho gives Lamine Yamal verdict: ‘He tried everything’
articles.summary: Jose Mourinho called the referee in Barca vs Madrid 'great'
articles.content:
Jose Mourinho gives Lamine Yamal verdict: ‘He tried everything’

Jose Mourinho called the referee in Barca vs Madrid 'great'

Last Update:

Jose Mourinho has called Real Madrid “extraordinary” after his side ended Barcelona’s perfect record in La Liga, singling out Marc Cucurella for coping with the “toughest match” of the full-back’s career against Ballon d’Or contender Lamine Yamal.

New signing Cucurella marked winger Yamal and played a part in the first of Kylian Mbappe’s goals in Madrid’s 2-1 away win, feeding Yan Diomande for a cross that was turned against the striker by opposition defender Gerard Martin’s attempted clearance.

“You can win by luck, by defending a lot… but we won comfortably and deservedly,” said Mourinho (via Marca), speaking after extinguishing Barca’s nine-match winning start to the Liga season to move three points behind the leaders.

“I’ve learned that I have an extraordinary group, with the quality and mentality to play. It’s a complete squad, they work hard, and they’re ready to win.”

Barcelona vs Real Madrid: Lamine Yamal ‘smart’

Spain sensation Yamal has eight goals and six assists in this season’s Liga but sent a glorious chance wide between Mbappe’s opener and the interval.

After Raphinha equalised during the second half, Yamal curled an effort wide and Mbappe struck his second to leave the 19-year-old looking rueful once the full-time whistle had sounded on the first clasico of the campaign.

“I always say that I only understand how good players are when I see them in front of me,” Mourinho said of the best result of his second spell in charge, having been reappointed before the start of the season.

“On television, I miss something. Ten metres away, I understand the quality of the players. [Yamal’s] very good, very difficult to play against.

“Besides being good, he’s smart. He tried everything. It’s the toughest match Cucu has had, against a very good player.”

Real Madrid boss Mourinho praises referee vs Barca

Mourinho warned that the win for Madrid, who are a point behind second-placed Atleti, will be meaningless if they do not prevail at midtable Racing Santander on Sunday (15:15 GMT).

“It was a great match,” said the Portuguese. “A high-level game – one that surely everyone who loves football stopped to watch, with two teams who played to win.

“I’m more concerned with speaking about my own team, but the lads played an extraordinary match – very organised, focused, with the courage to play out from the back against opponents who pressed a lot.

“We had chances to make it 2-0… Barcelona reacted strongly in the second half but we remained very calm and organised, and even at 1-1 we never lost our composure.

“Against great opponents and with a referee [Juan Martinez Munuera] who I think had a great game… it was a great match, a great victory.”

Real Madrid team vs Barcelona in el clasico

Andriy Lunin – who made several impressive saves – replaced Thibaut Courtois in one of five Madrid changes alongside the introductions of defenders Ibrahima Konate and Cucurella, midfielder Aurelien Tchouameni and winger Diomande.

Alvaro Carreras, Antonio Rudiger and Eduardo Camavinga moved to the bench. Vinicius Junior was suspended.

Newcastle, Brentford and Hull rose in the Premier League table

Newcastle visited Crystal Palace aiming to end a run of two consecutive defeats and Hull City were targeting a first win in seven matches in all competitions when the Tigers hosted Brentford on Sunday.

The Magpies had followed up a 4-1 thrashing at Coventry City with a 1-0 defeat at home to Aston Villa eight days earlier.

Palace had lost 5-0 at arch-rivals Brighton & Hove Albion a week earlier, while Brentford spurned a lead to suffer their first top-flight defeat of the season with a 2-1 home defeat to Liverpool on October 17.

You can also relive text updates as they happened from Sunday’s simultaneous games: Manchester United vs Bournemouth and Liverpool vs Brighton & Hove Albion.

Newcastle rose to seventh with the help of two goals inside 12 minutes shortly after the restart at Selhurst Park, where William Osula struck from Jacob Murphy’s cross and Harvey Barnes fired in from Amar Dedic’s delivery.

articles.summary: Florian Wirtz twisted his ankle in Liverpool vs Brighton
articles.content:
Wirtz on ankle injury and Liverpool win: ‘Things weren’t so good’

Florian Wirtz twisted his ankle in Liverpool vs Brighton

Last Update:

Liverpool midfielder Florian Wirtz says he is ignoring people who “judge” him and is “even happier” with Sunday’s 2-0 win at home to Brighton & Hove Albion because of the Reds’ run of two victories in their first six league games of the season.

Seeking a first home league win since April 25, Liverpool took a 17th-minute lead when one of Wirtz’s Germany teammates, Pascal Gross, applied the deciding touch to the £116 million playmaker’s shot, followed by Alexander Isak striking his sixth Premier League goal of the season four minutes later.

“It’s really enjoyable, I have to say,” Wirtz told BBC Sport, also suggesting that he will not be sidelined by an ankle injury that caused his substitution.

“Many things weren’t so good in the last month, so I’m even happier that it’s going well at the moment. We are on a good [path] to get where we want to be.”

“We had the right mentality [against Brighton]. Especially in the, first half or the first 30 minutes, we were on top of them and really good in the duels, also creating a lot of chances.”

Liverpool vs Brighton: Wirtz ‘just wants to play’

Liverpool broke their club record at the time to sign Wirtz from Leverkusen in June 2025, making his return of five goals and three assists in 33 league appearances seem another underwhelming part of their meek title defence.

“Maybe I’m just an interesting guy,” Wirtz said of scrutiny around his displays. “I just play my football – if people want to talk about or judge me, that’s their job.

“I’m not focusing on that; I just want to play football and I cannot do more.”

Wirtz scored his first goal of the campaign in the 4-3 home win over Villarreal in the Champions League on Tuesday.

“I would have preferred that the [first] goal [against Brighton] was given to me,” Wirtz reflected. “But it’s like this now.”

What’s next? Liverpool fixtures

Liverpool – perhaps without Wirtz – are next in action at home to Chelsea in the EFL Cup fourth round on October 28.

They then host defending champions Arsenal in the league on Sunday.

articles.title: ‘No hiding from tough situation’ says Carrick after latest Man Utd defeat
articles.summary: United are alarmingly close to the relegation zone
articles.content:
‘No hiding from tough situation’ says Carrick after latest Man Utd defeat

United are alarmingly close to the relegation zone

Last Update:

Manchester United boss Michael Carrick said there could be ‘no hiding’ from him or his players after their latest poor result in the Premier League.

A 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth left United 16th in the top flight and without a win in eight matches.

Carrick was applauded by fans at the end who turned on the club’s board and Jason Wilcox, the club’s director of football, instead.

Carrick had taken the decision to leave out captain Bruno Fernandes – who stayed on the bench throughout.

Carrick applauded fans on a slow lap of Old Trafford but insisted afterwards that he was not saying goodbye.

He told Sky Sports: “It’s difficult for me to have a day like this at this club and feel the emotion – the dynamic of what it was like today. Not for me personally but for Manchester United.

“I feel a lot of responsibility, I’ve been at the club a long time. It hurts an awful to to see us going through this at this moment in time.

“It wasn’t a farewell from me. I’m feeling it for my players, they’re going through a tough spell. Some of it we can help, some of it the situation unravels and the boys are feeling it at the moment.

“It’s a tough situation, there’s no hiding from it. What it looks like and what’s next I really don’t know.

“I will always do my best for the football club and I won’t change that now. I love what I do and I feel the responsibility – we’ll have to wait and see.”

United’s next three league games are against Chelsea, Aston Villa and Liverpool.

Former captain Gary Neville said on Sky Sports: “It is going to get ridiculously difficult for Michael Carrick to be Manchester United manager moving forward. That’s the problem the club have got.

“It is horrible to say that. I did think that last season that the club should have gone for the best manager they could have got and not given the job to Michael Carrick.

“Because I felt this might happen this quickly but this has gone very, very sour very quickly and the club is a mess.”

articles.title: Alvarez strike sees Atletico pile pressure on Barcelona ahead of Clasico
articles.summary: Alvarez scored for the second time in as many games.
articles.content:
Alvarez strike sees Atletico pile pressure on Barcelona ahead of Clasico

Alvarez scored for the second time in as many games.

Last Update:

Julian Alvarez scored his first home goal of the season as Atletico Madrid beat Deportivo La Coruna 1-0 to move Diego Simeone’s men within two points of LaLiga leaders Barcelona.

Alvarez, who tried to force through a move to Barca in the summer, got off the mark for the campaign in midweek with a goal in the 1-1 Champions League draw at Stuttgart.

And he followed that effort up with a simple finish at the Metropolitano that put the pressure on Barca ahead of their Clasico with Real Madrid on Sunday.

Alvarez turned home from Alejandro Grimaldo’s cross three minutes into the second half, his close-range effort proving decisive as Atletico made it eight wins from 10 to start their league season.

Georges Mikautadze scored a 96th-minute winner as Villarreal won 2-1 at neighbours Valencia.

Pepelu’s emphatic penalty gave Valencia the lead, which looked to have been doubled when Cesar Tarrega fired in after Villarreal failed to clear a corner.

However, that was ruled out for offside and Alexander Freeman then levelled by heading home Sergi Cardona’s cross.

The game looked to have turned back in Valencia’s favour as Pape Gueye was sent off for an elbow on Jose Gaya.

Yet the hosts were also reduced to 10 men when Harvey Elliott received two yellows in succession for dissent, and Villarreal claimed the derby spoils at the death as Alberto Moleiro’s excellent pass was collected by Mikautadze, who emphatically converted to leave Valencia with just six points from 10 games.

Racing Santander beat Espanyol 2-1, and Elche were 3-0 winners at Rayo Vallecano.

Lazio go top, Roma stay unbeaten after thriller

Lazio moved top of Serie A with a 2-1 win over Parma as their city rivals Roma maintained their unbeaten start with a thrilling 3-3 draw at Napoli.

Gustav Isaksen had a first-half goal ruled out for offside for Lazio, but Kenneth Taylor’s effort and an own goal from Diego Carlos proved enough to secure the points.

They are three points ahead of defending champions Inter Milan in the Scudetto race ahead of the Nerazzurri’s clash with Fiorentina on Sunday.

Roma are four points off the pace but, like their arch rivals, are still yet to taste defeat after twice coming from behind to draw with Napoli.

Frank Anguissa’s stunning overhead kick put Napoli in front before their lead was doubled by Scott McTominay when he nodded in on the rebound after seeing an initial close-range header kept out.

But Matias Soule’s fine long-range strike saw Roma pull one back, with Leonardo Balerdi then lashing home a leveller from point-blank range.

McTominay restored Napoli’s lead with an unerring long-distance effort into the bottom-left corner, only for Balerdi to rescue a point by heading home his second.

Elsewhere, Como beat Sassuolo 2-0 and Bologna won at Cagliari by the same scoreline.

Dortmund return to summit

Borussia Dortmund moved back to the summit of the Bundesliga with a 1-0 win over Eintracht Frankfurt.

Maximilian Beier was the difference as his 80th-minute goal secured the points, sending Dortmund three clear of Bayern Munich ahead of their meeting with third-placed Freiburg on Sunday.

Romulo Cardoso scored twice as RB Leipzig ran out 4-0 winners over Elversberg, while two penalties from Niklas Fullkrug helped Werder Bremen beat Mainz 3-2.

Paderborn were 1-0 winners over Hamburg, their victory seeing Union Berlin drop into the bottom two after a 1-1 draw at Augsburg in which both teams had a man sent off. Schalke drew 0-0 with Cologne.

In Ligue 1, Paris FC missed the chance to at least temporarily go top of the table as they were beaten 2-1 by Lens.

Florian Thauvin equalised for Lens after being teed up by Thorgan Hazard, with the roles then reversed as the latter fired home from Thauvin’s cross to complete the turnaround.

articles.title: De Zerbi labels Tottenham as ‘complete team’ after Spurs’ derby win at Chelsea
articles.summary: Spurs are up to 12th after successive wins.
articles.content:
De Zerbi labels Tottenham as ‘complete team’ after Spurs’ derby win at Chelsea

Spurs are up to 12th after successive wins.

Last Update:

Roberto De Zerbi hailed Tottenham as a “complete team” after they claimed a 2-0 London derby win over Chelsea.

Having gotten off the mark on Monday with their first Premier League win of the season over Coventry City, Tottenham prevailed away at Stamford Bridge for the first time since 2018, though they received a helping hand from Chelsea goalkeeper Mike Penders.

Penders, filling in for the injured Emiliano Martinez, endured a Premier League debut to forget as he punched a corner into his own net 13 minutes from the end of normal time.

Chelsea star Cole Palmer was then sent off for a second bookable offence, before Mathys Tel made sure of the points with a fine individual effort.

And De Zerbi was effusive in his praise of his players after they secured back-to-back wins to move up to 12th in the  table.

“It was a big moment for the fans, the club and the players also,” De Zerbi told Sky Sports.

“They deserved this win, they prepared very well. We are improving a lot, we are improving in the mentality, in the group and the relationships with the players and then we are improving on the pitch.

“Against Aston Villa, Everton for 30 minutes we were playing very well. Maybe no goals, no finishing good enough to score and maybe in the first bad moment we changed mentality. Now it is a complete team. The players are playing better, we improved in the style.

“When we stay for dinner and stay together in the dressing room I see a different group, a different relationship and different atmosphere among the players.

“The character was today great but we have many, many new players. The players who stayed here last season, two or three seasons ago, they suffered the last results, two times 17th position, we are working to change the last part of the history of the club.

“We are lucky because we have many great people in the dressing room, many great players. I think if we work hard we can do something important.

“I have to believe for sure in this group. I never lost the confidence in my players. The week in Marbella [during the international break], to speak better face to face, to open ourselves and remove the mask it is important. It is important for the spirit, the belief. The atmosphere inside the dressing room is maybe more important than the tactics.”

Chelsea came into the game on the back of successive victories, but head coach Xabi Alonso conceded the Blues were far below their best.

“We are all disappointed with the result, with the performance collectively and individually we were not at our best level,” Alonso told Sky.

“It was about the first goal and it went their way and with 10 men it was difficult but we can do better.

“Chances were the main thing, they had few and we had few. We spoke at half time we had to be patient and be mature. We can do better.

“We wanted to have this fluidity in the middle. We wanted the pockets filed with Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers. There were situations but overall we have to do better.”
